1Quick start

This chapter describes the shortest path from opening Cam Hub to the first live picture. Without a device at hand, the sample cameras can be used to try the app.

Before you begin

ItemDescription
NetworkCam Hub connects directly to the network address of the device and does not use a cloud service of the manufacturer. The iPhone or iPad must be on the same local network as the device, or must be able to reach its address.
IP address of the deviceThe address is listed in the connection list of the router or in the manufacturer's own app. It can also be found with the network scan; see “Finding devices with the network scan”.
Account of the deviceUsually the administrator account that was created when the device was first set up. On the device, the account needs the permissions for the functions to be used, for example live view, recording playback and PTZ control.
Local Network permissionOn first use, the system asks whether Cam Hub may find and connect to devices on the local network. Without this permission, Cam Hub cannot connect to devices. The permission can be turned on later under Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network › Cam Hub.

Shortest path to a live picture

  1. Tap the Devices tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the device list. When no device has been added yet, it shows No Devices.

  2. Tap the ＋ button in the top-right corner.

    Check: A menu opens that contains Add Device.

  3. Select Add Device.

    Check: The screen shows the add-device form.

  4. Enter the address of the device in the IP address or hostname field.

    Check: The Add button in the top-right corner is available.

  5. Enter the account of the device in the Username and Password fields.

    Check: Connect using shows Auto-detect. No change is needed.

  6. Tap Add in the top-right corner.

    Check: The form shows Connecting to device…. When the connection succeeds, the form closes and the new device appears in the device list.

  7. Tap the newly added device in the device list.

    Check: The device page shows the device information and a thumbnail for each channel.

  8. Tap the thumbnail of a channel that is enabled.

    Check: The screen shows the live picture of that camera.

If the connection fails, see “When adding fails: the checklist”. If a thumbnail does not open, see Chapter 4, “The Devices tab and channels” and Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”. To watch several cameras at once, see Chapter 8, “LiveView Mix”.

Trying the app without a device

At the bottom of the add-device form, Add Demo Cameras creates two sample cameras that draw their own picture. No device and no sign-in are needed, so they can be used to try live view and LiveView Mix. The sample cameras have no recording playback.

Delete the sample device before connecting real equipment

The sample device counts as a recorder. It uses up the recorder allowance and the enabled-channel allowance of the free plan. For deleting a device, see Chapter 4, “The Devices tab and channels”; for the allowances, see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.

2The tabs and basic behaviour

The bottom of the screen holds five tabs, from left to right: LiveView Mix, Live, Devices, Tools and Settings. This chapter describes the purpose of each tab and its main controls.

The tabs at a glance

TabPurposeDetails
LiveView MixPlaces cameras from different devices on one wall, with optional clocks, pictures and control buttons.Chapter 8, “LiveView Mix”
LiveShows the live wall with all enabled channels of one device.Chapter 5, “The Live tab and the Full Screen Wall”
DevicesAdds and manages devices. Opening a device shows its channels.Chapter 3, “Adding a device”, Chapter 4, “The Devices tab and channels”
ToolsScans the network to find cameras and recorders.Chapter 12, “The Tools tab”, “Finding devices with the network scan”
SettingsPlans, default quality, picture, backup and restore, sharing cameras, language and reset.Chapter 13, “Settings”

What opens when the app starts

The app always starts on the LiveView Mix tab. It does not return to the tab that was open when the app was last closed. To start on the live wall of one device, or directly on the full-screen LiveView Mix wall, change Open on launch in the Settings tab; see “LiveView Mix and Open on launch”.

Appearance and language

The app uses a dark appearance only; there is no light or dark setting. The language follows the system language by default and can be changed in Settings; see “Language”.

Turning the device

The app does not lock the screen orientation. On an iPhone it works upright and in both landscape orientations; on an iPad it works in all four orientations. The full-screen wall lays itself out again when the shape of the screen changes; see “The full-screen wall”.

Screen, background and notifications

While live or recorded video is on the screen, the display does not switch itself off. When the app leaves the foreground, every live stream stops and no sound plays in the background. When the app returns, the tiles connect again and a recording that was playing resumes where it stopped. The app sends no notifications and asks for no notification permission.

3Adding a device

Adding a device requires its address, its account and a connection method. By default, Cam Hub identifies the device itself; ONVIF or a supported brand from the list can be selected instead.

The Add Device form

Path: Devices › ＋ › Add Device

FieldDescriptionDefault
Name (optional)The name under which the device is shown in Cam Hub. When left empty, the model reported by the device is used.Empty
IP address or hostnameRequired. The network address of the device.Empty
HTTP PortThe port of the control interface of the device, used by auto-detection and ONVIF connections. When the management interface of the device does not use 80, enter the actual port, for example 2020 on some ONVIF devices or 5000 for recorder software on some network storage devices.80
RTSP PortThe port of the video stream.554
UsernameThe sign-in account of the device.admin
PasswordThe sign-in password of the device. The password is stored in the keychain of the device.Empty
Connect usingAuto-detect, ONVIF, or a supported brand from the list. For the choice, see “Choosing the connection method”.Auto-detect

  1. Tap the Devices tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the device list.

  2. Tap the ＋ button in the top-right corner. When the list is empty, the Add Device button in the middle of the screen can be used instead.

    Check: A menu opens that contains Add Device.

  3. Select Add Device.

    Check: The screen shows the add-device form with Device, Credentials and Connect using.

  4. Optional: enter a name for the device in the Name (optional) field.

    Check: The field shows the name, which is later shown in the device list.

  5. Enter the address of the device in the IP address or hostname field, for example 192.168.1.64.

    Check: The Add button in the top-right corner is available.

  6. When the device does not use 80 and 554 as ports, change the HTTP Port and RTSP Port fields.

    Check: Both fields show the ports that the device uses.

  7. Enter the account of the device in the Username and Password fields.

    Check: Both fields are filled in. The password is masked with dots.

  8. Select the connection method in the Connect using menu. In most cases, keep Auto-detect.

    Check: The menu shows the selected connection method. When a brand from the list is selected, the form gains two fields for the number of cameras and the path.

  9. Tap Add in the top-right corner.

    Check: The form shows Connecting to device…. When the connection succeeds, the form closes and the new device appears in the device list.

While the connection is made, the Add button is unavailable and the form cannot be closed with a downward swipe. After connecting, Cam Hub identifies whether the device is a recorder or a single camera, reads the channel list and stores the device.

The free plan enables only the channels within its allowance; the remaining channels are shown as Disabled. When the number of recorders allowed by the plan has been reached, the plans page opens. For the allowances, see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.

Address and account of a stored device cannot be edited

A stored device can only be renamed. When the password changes, add the device again with the same address, HTTP port and username; the existing device and its stored password are updated in place. When the IP address changes, the new address is treated as a different device, and a recorder also counts against the recorder allowance. In that case, delete the old device first (see Chapter 4, “The Devices tab and channels”) and add the new address.

Choosing the connection method

The Connect using menu offers three kinds of options:

  • Auto-detect (default): Cam Hub identifies the device itself. It first tries the manufacturer protocols that are built in, and uses ONVIF only when none of them answers. This option is sufficient for most devices.
  • ONVIF: skips auto-detection and uses the open ONVIF protocol. Use it for cameras that Cam Hub does not recognize, or to use ONVIF on a device that also supports its own protocol. ONVIF must be turned on at the device; when the device has a separate ONVIF user list, a user must be created there. The HTTP Port must be the ONVIF service port of the device. Whether recording playback and PTZ control are available depends on what the device offers.
  • A supported brand from the list: connects directly over RTSP, using the stream paths documented for that brand. Use it when ONVIF is turned off at the device. After a brand is selected, the form gains two fields:
    • Cameras: a number from 1 to 64. With 1, the device is added as a single camera; with 2 or more, it is added as a recorder and counts against the recorder allowance.
    • The path field: when left blank, Cam Hub tries the documented paths of that brand in turn and keeps the one that the device answers. Fill it in only to specify a particular path.

Some brands need a dedicated camera or ONVIF account, created in the manufacturer's app or web interface, before RTSP works; the administrator account alone may be refused. For some brands, the paths vary by model or firmware, so the first attempt may not match. For the list of supported brands and the notes on each, see Chapter 16, “Supported brands and connection methods”.

A connection through a brand from the list provides live view only

This connection method has no recording playback and no PTZ control. SD and HD may be the same stream.

Device control uses HTTP only

Device control (identifying the device, reading the channel list, searching recordings) uses http://address:port. A device that accepts HTTPS only cannot be added at present.

Failure messages differ for a connection through a brand from the list

When the device cannot be reached or times out, only Something went wrong. Please try again. is shown. With this connection method, Not a supported device. means that none of the candidate paths of the brand returned a stream. Common causes are a wrong RTSP port or a video stream that is turned off at the device.

When it is unclear whether a device can be used, tap Compatibility reference in the form to see the supported and unsupported devices.

When adding fails: the checklist

When adding fails, the form shows the error message in red and lists Things to check first below it. The order of the list depends on the kind of failure, with the most likely cause first. Work through the items from top to bottom, then tap Add again.

Error messageChecks (from top to bottom)
Device unreachable. Check the address and your network.
  1. Check the IP address. Look it up on the router or in the manufacturer's own app, or use the scan in the Tools tab.
  2. Connect the phone to the same Wi-Fi network as the device. Guest networks, a separate VLAN, or client isolation on the router block the connection.
  3. Allow Local Network access: Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network › Cam Hub
  4. Turn off any VPN on the phone while adding a device on the home network.
  5. Make sure the device is powered on and its network cable or Wi-Fi is connected.
  6. Check the HTTP and RTSP ports. The usual ones are 80 and 554; some devices use 8000, 8080, 8899 or 37777.
  7. In the device settings, turn on ONVIF and RTSP. When the device has a separate ONVIF user list, create a user there.
Wrong username or password.
  1. Sign in once on the web page of the device itself to check the username and password. They are case-sensitive.
  2. A brand-new device must be activated first, usually by setting an administrator password, before any app can sign in.
  3. Too many wrong attempts can lock the account for a while, often about 30 minutes. Wait, then try once with the correct password.
  4. Set the clock of the device to the correct time, for example with network time. A clock that is off by minutes makes ONVIF sign-in fail.
  5. In the device settings, turn on ONVIF and RTSP. When the device has a separate ONVIF user list, create a user there.
  6. Try a different Connect using option: ONVIF, or the brand of the camera from the list.
Not a supported device.
  1. Try a different Connect using option: ONVIF, or the brand of the camera from the list.
  2. In the device settings, turn on ONVIF and RTSP. When the device has a separate ONVIF user list, create a user there.
  3. Check the HTTP and RTSP ports.
  4. Some devices work only through the cloud app of the manufacturer and offer no local connection. Cam Hub cannot connect to those devices.
Too many requests just now. Try again in a minute.
  1. Wait a minute, then try once more.
  2. When the request is still refused, the account may be locked temporarily after too many wrong attempts, often for about 30 minutes. Wait, then try once with the correct password.
Something went wrong. Please try again. and any other message not listed above
  1. Check the IP address.
  2. Connect the phone to the same Wi-Fi network as the device.
  3. Check the HTTP and RTSP ports.
  4. Sign in once on the web page of the device itself to check the username and password.
  5. Try a different Connect using option: ONVIF, or the brand of the camera from the list.
  6. Some devices work only through the cloud app of the manufacturer and offer no local connection. Cam Hub cannot connect to those devices.

When the failure persists after all items have been worked through, the experimental device report can be used; see “Device report (experimental)”.

Device report (experimental)

Experimental feature, no guarantee of support

The device report is an experimental feature. It may change or be removed at any time. Sending a report does not mean that the developer will add support for the device, and there is no guarantee of a reply, a fix or a timeline. Some devices cannot be supported by design, for example because of closed or proprietary protocols, cloud-only operation, licensing or encryption restrictions, or hardware limits. The feature is not a customer-support or urgent-help channel.

Collecting the details signs in to the device with the account and password that were entered. Failed sign-ins are counted, and may be logged, by the device. When the password may be wrong, correct it first as described in “When adding fails: the checklist” instead of trying repeatedly.

The Send details to the developer button, marked Experimental, appears below the checklist only after adding has failed; it is not shown when adding succeeds. The feature runs only when the button is tapped. It checks the device with read-only requests and assembles a text report for review. Cam Hub never uploads the report by itself; the report is sent only if the person chooses to email it from their own mail account.

Prerequisite: the checklist in “When adding fails: the checklist” has been worked through, and the address, username and password in the form are the ones that the device uses.

  1. In the form of the failed attempt, scroll to the checklist and tap Send details to the developer below it.

    Check: On first use, the screen shows the Device Report page with the full notice Before you collect details.

  2. Read the notice and tap I understand — collect details.

    Check: The screen shows Collecting details… and the progress of each check.

  3. Wait until the collection is complete.

    Check: What we found lists the likely causes and what to try first, in plain language. When nothing stands out, the screen shows Nothing obvious stands out.

  4. Under What to include, switch off the items that should not be sent.

    Check: The text in the The report section updates immediately.

  5. Review the full text in the The report section.

    Check: The report is plain text and is always in English. Data that was masked automatically is replaced by a mask marker.

  6. Tap Email to developer.

    Check: The screen opens the mail composer with the report in the message.

  7. Check the message and send it.

    Check: The mail composer closes and the report page is shown again.

  8. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The report page closes and the add-device form is shown again.

  • After the notice has been confirmed once, the report page shows only a short reminder at the top, with About this feature to read the full notice again.
  • During the collection, Stop in the top-left corner ends it early. What has been found so far is kept, the screen shows You stopped the collection, so this report is partial. Nothing has been sent. and offers Collect again.
  • What to include has five items: Network, HTTP fingerprint, Protocol probes, RTSP and video and App trace, each marked with a letter. The findings and the report header are always included.
  • Besides Email to developer, the report can be copied with Copy or passed on with Share…. A copy stays on this device only and expires after about 2 minutes.
  • When no mail account is set up, the screen shows Mail isn't set up on this device: the full report is copied to the clipboard, the mail app opens with the start of the report, and the full report must be pasted into the message.
  • The report leaves the device only when it is sent. Nothing is sent unless you choose to send the email. Your password is never included.

Sign-in behavior

During the collection, requests that need a sign-in are sent one at a time until the device has accepted or refused the credentials. After the device has refused them, the report sends no further sign-ins. When the failed attempt that led to the report was itself a refused sign-in (Wrong username or password.), the report does not try to sign in at all, so that the account is not locked by the device. The collection sends only read-only requests and does not change any setting on the device.

What the report contains and does not contain

  • Contains: the versions of the app and the system, the model identifier of the phone, the language setting, the selected connection method, the device address (the last part of a private network address is masked with x; for a public address only its class is given), the ports, the error code of the failed attempt, the detected brand and model, open ports, the headers and structure of the answers of the device (masked), the encoding and parameters of the stream, the difference in clock and time zone, and the steps that were run with their results.
  • Does not contain: the password, the username, the name given to the device, a public address or dynamic domain name, the hardware address of the network adapter, email addresses, tokens and other identifying data, pictures and video. Of a long serial number, only the last four characters are kept.
  • Masking is automatic, and each masked item leaves a marker. The report should still be reviewed before it is sent, and any item can be switched off.
Questions in the email

The body of the email contains several questions, among them the brand and model as printed on the label of the device, the firmware version, the kind of device, the difference between what was expected and what happened, whether the manufacturer's own app or a media player shows the device, and an RTSP address that opens in a media player (with the username, password and address removed first). Answering them helps the developer to assess the device.

Saved reports

Each report is saved on this device, and the five most recent are kept. An entry that shows the saved date, for the previous report, appears below the error message; tapping it opens the report again. A saved report shows its content as it was saved and cannot be switched item by item; to choose the content again, collect the details again.

To delete the saved reports:

  1. At the bottom of the report page, tap Delete saved reports.

    Check: The screen shows the dialog Delete all saved reports?, which explains that every device report saved on this device is removed and that a report that was already emailed is not affected.

  2. Tap Delete saved reports in the dialog.

    Check: All saved reports are deleted. The report on the screen is only shown there and is not saved again.

Finding devices with the network scan

Location: the Tools tab at the bottom of the screen.

When the IP address of a device is not known, the Tools tab can scan a network range. The scan probes the four common ports 80, 554, 8000 and 37777 and lists the addresses that answer.

  1. Tap the Tools tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: In the Subnet section, the This device row shows the current network address and mask, for example 192.168.1.10/24. The address field and Range are filled in with the current network.

  2. Optional: to scan a different network, enter the network in the address field, for example 192.168.1.0, and select the range in the Range menu.

    Check: Below the field, a line shows the network and the number of hosts that will be scanned, for example Will scan 192.168.1.0/24 · 254 hosts.

  3. Tap Scan.

    Check: The screen shows the progress Scanned 120 of 254, and the button changes to Stop.

  4. Wait until the scan ends; to end it early, tap Stop.

    Check: Found Devices lists the addresses that answered, with the open ports of each address in the row. When nothing was found, the screen shows No devices found yet.

  5. Tap a row in the results.

    Check: The screen opens the add-device form with the address already entered in the IP address or hostname field. The other fields keep their defaults; continue with the steps in “The Add Device form”.

  • Range runs from /26 (smallest) to /16 (largest). When a range holds more than 1,024 addresses, the scan samples them evenly instead of probing each one.
  • When the address field or the range differs from the current network, Use my subnet appears; tapping it restores the current network.
  • When the address field has an invalid format, the screen shows Enter a subnet like 192.168.1 or 192.168.1.0.
  • A result carries over only the address, not the open ports. When the HTTP port of the device is not 80, it must be changed by hand. After the device has been added, the screen returns to the Tools tab, not to the device list.
Limits of the scan results

The scan finds only devices that answer on camera ports. It cannot tell a camera from a recorder; the type is confirmed when the device is added. Open ports and any server name give a hint about the manufacturer.

When a scan has finished completely without any result, the screen shows If your cameras are on this network, check that Cam Hub is allowed to find devices on your local network in the system privacy settings. When the Local Network permission is denied, the scan shows no error; its result is empty as well. Check that the permission is turned on: Settings › Privacy & Security › Local Network › Cam Hub.

4The Devices tab and channels

The Devices tab lists every recorder and camera that has been added. Opening a device shows its channels as live thumbnails. From there, channels are renamed, disabled, paused or shown in a full-screen wall, and the limits of the plan decide which channels can show a picture.

The device list

Path: Devices tab at the bottom of the screen.

Each row shows the name of the device, its model and its address. The icon on the left marks a recorder or a camera. On the right, a connection indicator sits above a label that names the type: Recorder or Camera. The indicator reports whether the device accepts a connection on its HTTP port. The check starts every time the row appears on the screen and waits for an answer for about 4 seconds.

IndicatorMeaning
Small spinning circleThe check is running.
Green Wi-Fi symbolThe device answered (Reachable).
Red, crossed-out Wi-Fi symbolThe device did not answer (Can't reach this device — check the network or firewall). The device may be switched off, on a different network, or blocked by a firewall.
The indicator tests the HTTP port only

A device that does not accept connections on the stored HTTP port can show the red symbol while its video works, for example a camera that was added through a brand from the list. The sample cameras use the address demo, which is not a device on the network, and always show the red symbol.

Opening a device

  1. Tap the Devices tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the device list. When no device has been added, the screen shows No Devices, the text Add your first camera or recorder to get started. and the Add Device button; see Chapter 3, “Adding a device”.

  2. Tap a row in the list.

    Check: The device page opens; see “The device page”.

Changing the order of the devices

  1. Tap Edit in the top-left corner. The button is shown only while at least one device exists.

    Check: A drag handle appears on the right of every row, and the button now reads Done.

  2. Touch the handle of a row and drag the row to its new position.

    Check: The row stays at the new position.

  3. Tap Done.

    Check: The list leaves edit mode. The order is stored. The device selection list in the Live tab uses the same order.

Deleting a device

Deleting removes the device from Cam Hub. The device itself is not changed.

  1. Swipe left on the row of the device.

    Check: A Delete button with a trash symbol appears on the right of the row. Even a full swipe only opens the confirmation; nothing is deleted without it.

  2. Tap Delete.

    Check: The dialog Delete this device? appears. It names the device and the number of its cameras, and states that the saved password is removed as well and that the action cannot be undone.

  3. Tap Delete in the dialog. Tap Cancel instead to keep the device.

    Check: The row disappears. The device, its channels and its saved password are removed from this iPhone or iPad. The device is also removed from the LiveView Mix wall, and from the choices of the Live tab and of Open on launch when it was selected there.

A deleted recorder no longer counts against the number of recorders that the plan allows; see “Plan limits and enabling channels”. To add the device again, see Chapter 3, “Adding a device”.

The device page

The device page shows an information card at the top and, below it, the channels of the device as thumbnails. The title is the name of the device. The thumbnails are arranged in as many columns as fit on the screen.

  • Information card: shows the name and the type of the device and the rows Model, IP address, Port (the HTTP port), Serial number, Firmware and Cameras (the number of channels). The serial number and the firmware appear only when the device reports them.
  • Thumbnails: a recorder shows one thumbnail per channel; a standalone camera has one channel and shows one thumbnail. The lower-left corner of every thumbnail shows the number and the name of the channel. The thumbnails use SD or HD according to Settings › Default quality › Multiple cameras (SD unless changed). A change in Settings applies to this page at once; the page has no SD/HD button of its own.
  • Refresh: Cam Hub reads the channel list from the device when the page opens and again when the page is pulled down. Names and online states are updated, channels that the device has added appear, and channels that the device has removed disappear. A new channel is enabled only when the plan allows it; otherwise it is shown as Disabled. Names that were set in Cam Hub are kept. When the device does not answer, the list stays as it was and no message is shown.
  • No channels: when the device reports no channel, the page shows No cameras found.

The three buttons at the top right are, from left to right: the black-bar button, Full Screen Wall and Rename (pencil).

Hiding or showing the details

  1. Tap the arrow on the right of the information card (Hide details).

    Check: The rows below the name disappear, and the arrow changes direction (Show details). Tapping it again shows the rows. The choice is stored for each device.

Renaming a device

  1. Tap the pencil button (Rename) at the top right of the device page.

    Check: The dialog Rename Device opens, with the current name in the Name field.

  2. Enter the new name in the Name field.

    Check: The field shows the new name.

  3. Tap Save.

    Check: The title of the page and the device list show the new name. An empty name is ignored and the old name stays. The name is stored in Cam Hub only; the device is not changed.

Changing the handling of black bars on this page

The black-bar button is the left one of the three buttons. Each tap selects the next of three modes; after the third mode the first one returns.

ModeEffect
DefaultThe whole picture is shown. Black bars appear where the shape of the picture differs from the shape of the thumbnail.
Enlarge to fillThe picture is enlarged in proportion until it fills the thumbnail. The edges of the picture are cut off.
Stretch to fillThe picture is stretched until it fills the thumbnail. The picture is distorted.

  1. Tap the left button of the three buttons at the top right.

    Check: All thumbnails change to the next mode, and the icon of the button changes to match the current mode.

The first mode comes from Settings › Picture › Black bars. A change made on this page applies to this page only and is not stored.

What a thumbnail shows

The content of a thumbnail depends on the state of the channel. The table lists the states in the order in which Cam Hub decides between them. A tap opens the single-camera view only for an online channel that is enabled, within the plan and not paused; see Chapter 6, “Single-camera view”.

ThumbnailMeaningTapping the thumbnail
Grey, with a pause symbol and PausedThe video of the channel was paused by hand. The channel does not stream, and it keeps its place in the plan.Nothing happens.
DisabledThe channel is disabled. It does not stream and does not use a place in the plan.Nothing happens.
Not in your plan with a lockThe channel is enabled, but the plan does not cover it.The plans screen opens; see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.
Live pictureThe channel is enabled, within the plan, not paused, and the device reports a signal. A spinner shows while the connection is made.The single-camera view opens.
Failure message on a dark backgroundThe channel is in order, but the stream could not be opened. Cam Hub tries again by itself.The single-camera view opens.
Grey, with a crossed-out camera and No signalThe device reports that the channel has no signal.Nothing happens.

Not every device reports a missing signal for each channel. For channels of such devices, a stream that cannot be opened shows a failure message instead of No signal.

Hide offline cameras affects the walls only

The setting Hide offline cameras removes cameras without a signal from the live walls. The device page always lists every channel and shows the ones without a signal in grey. LiveView Mix walls are not affected by the setting.

Channel options (long press)

A long press on a thumbnail opens a menu with the options below.

Menu itemEffectUses a place in the plan
Rename cameraSets a name of your own for the channel.None.
Your plan › Disable or EnableOnly the item that matches the current state is offered. A disabled channel does not stream and shows Disabled.A disabled channel releases its place.
Bandwidth › Pause Video or Resume VideoOffered for channels of a recorder only. A paused channel stops streaming, which saves bandwidth, and shows Paused.A paused channel keeps its place.

Renaming a channel

  1. Long press the thumbnail of the channel.

    Check: The menu of the channel opens.

  2. Tap Rename camera.

    Check: A dialog opens with the current name in the Name field and the buttons Cancel, Use Device Name and Save.

  3. Enter the new name and tap Save.

    Check: The lower-left corner of the thumbnail shows the new name. The same name is used on the Live tab, on LiveView Mix walls and as the title of the single-camera view.

  4. To return to the name that the device reports, repeat the first two steps and tap Use Device Name.

    Check: The thumbnail shows the name of the device again.

A name set in Cam Hub is not overwritten when the channel list is refreshed, and it is included in backups; see Chapter 10, “Sharing and backup”.

Pausing and resuming the video of a recorder channel

  1. Long press the thumbnail of a channel of a recorder.

    Check: The menu shows the section Bandwidth.

  2. Tap Pause Video.

    Check: The thumbnail turns grey and shows Paused. Every screen that shows this channel treats it as paused.

  3. To resume, long press the thumbnail again and tap Resume Video.

    Check: The live picture returns.

Plan limits and enabling channels

A channel is either enabled or disabled. An enabled channel uses one place of the plan. Only enabled channels within the limits of the plan show a picture; an enabled channel beyond the limits shows Not in your plan. The limits are listed below; the plans themselves are described in Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.

PlanStandalone camerasChannels of recordersRecorders that can be added
FreeAt most 2 enabled channels in total, counting cameras and recorder channels together. Enabled recorder channels must all belong to the same recorder.1
Camera planEnabled cameras up to the limit of the plan: 8, 16 or unlimited.As on the free plan: 2 enabled channels, all on one recorder.1
NVR planAs on the free plan: 2 enabled cameras.Every channel of the recorders that the plan covers.2, 4 or unlimited
  • Both plans can be held together. The two limits apply independently: the camera plan raises the limit for standalone cameras, and the NVR plan raises the number of recorders whose channels are all usable.
  • A control panel of a LiveView Mix wall counts as one camera against the camera limit; see Chapter 8, “LiveView Mix”.
  • A recorder counts toward the number of recorders as soon as it has been added, whether or not any of its channels is enabled. The sample cameras count like real devices.
  • When a plan ends or its limits fall below the number of enabled channels, the stored choices are kept. The channels beyond the limits show Not in your plan: standalone cameras keep their picture first, then recorder channels, each in the order in which the devices were added and in the order of the channel numbers.
  • When both limits are unlimited, every channel is enabled automatically, and the page Choose which cameras show is not offered.

Enabling a disabled channel

Prerequisite: the thumbnail of the channel shows Disabled.

  1. Long press the thumbnail of the disabled channel.

    Check: The menu shows Enable below Your plan.

  2. Tap Enable.

    Check: When the plan has a free place, the thumbnail starts to show the live picture; the procedure ends here. When the limit has been reached, the plans screen opens with a message and the channel stays disabled. The message is You've reached the Free plan's limit of 2 enabled cameras. for a standalone camera (the same text appears at the limit of a camera plan) and Unlock every channel with an NVR plan. for a recorder channel.

  3. Close the plans screen.

    Check: The device page is shown again.

  4. Long press the thumbnail of an enabled channel that is not needed and tap Disable.

    Check: The thumbnail shows Disabled, and its place in the plan is free.

  5. Repeat the first two steps for the channel that should be shown.

    Check: The thumbnail shows the live picture.

Choosing which cameras show

Path: Settings › Choose which cameras show

This page lists the channels of all devices in one place, so that the places of the plan can be assigned across devices without opening each device page. The item is offered only while at least one of the two limits of the plan applies.

  1. Tap the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the settings.

  2. In the Subscription section, tap Choose which cameras show.

    Check: The page License opens. The section Your plan shows the rows Cameras (for example 2 cameras or Unlimited) and Recorders, and the note Turn on the cameras you want to watch. The Free plan shows 2 cameras on a single recorder. Below it, one section per device lists every channel with its number, its name and a switch.

  3. Turn off the switch of a channel that is not needed.

    Check: The switch is off. The channel is disabled and its place in the plan is free. Turning a switch off is always possible.

  4. Turn on the switch of the channel that should be shown.

    Check: The switch is on when the plan has a free place. When it has not, the plans screen opens with a message and the switch stays off. On the free plan, the message On the Free plan, the cameras you show must all be on one recorder. appears when a channel of a second recorder is turned on.

  5. Tap the back button in the top-left corner to leave the page.

    Check: The choices apply everywhere: walls and the device pages show a picture for the enabled channels within the plan only.

When no device has been added, the page shows No Devices and Add a device first, then choose its cameras here.

The full-screen wall of a device

The full-screen wall shows all enabled channels of one device edge to edge. It opens from the device page and from the Live tab (see “The Full Screen Wall”), and it follows the way in which the iPhone is held: upright, the thumbnails keep their 16:9 shape and are stacked in rows of one or two (see the Layout button below); sideways, two rows fill the height. A device with only one enabled channel shows that camera over the whole screen.

  1. Tap the Full Screen Wall button (second of the three buttons) at the top right of the device page.

    Check: The wall covers the screen. It shows the enabled channels of the device; channels beyond the plan show Not in your plan. When no channel is enabled, the screen shows No enabled cameras and Enable cameras on the device page.

  2. When more channels exist than fit on the screen, scroll the wall vertically in upright orientation, or swipe sideways in landscape orientation.

    Check: The next channels or the next page appear. When the wall is divided into pages, dots at the bottom show the current page.

  3. Tap a thumbnail that shows a picture.

    Check: A close-up of that camera opens over the wall, with Back and the camera name at the top.

  4. Tap Back at the top left of the close-up.

    Check: The wall is shown again.

  5. Tap Close (the cross at the top left of the wall).

    Check: The screen returns to the device page or to the Live tab.

Button at the top of the wallFunction
Close (top left)Closes the wall.
SD or HDSwitches all cameras of the wall at once (Switch all cameras to HD or Switch all cameras to SD). The text on the button is the current quality. The wall starts with the quality of Settings › Default quality › Multiple cameras. The change is not stored.
LayoutSwitches between one and two thumbnails per row. This choice is stored.
Black-bar buttonCycles through Default, Enlarge to fill and Stretch to fill, as on the device page. The change is not stored.
  • Close-up: the picture uses the quality of Settings › Default quality › Single camera (HD unless changed), and the buttons of the wall are not shown. Spread two fingers to enlarge the picture up to 5 times, drag to move it while it is enlarged, and double-tap to switch between normal size and 2 times.
  • Speaker (lower left): appears when the camera sends sound; see “Snapshot, sound and quality”.
  • Camera control (lower right): appears when the camera can be moved or zoomed; see “PTZ control: moving the camera”.
  • Recordings (top right): appears for devices that support playback. It opens the single-camera view of the camera over the wall, with Done in the top-right corner to return; see Chapter 7, “Recording playback and speed”.
  • The setting Edge-to-Edge Video and the setting Hide offline cameras apply to the wall. A tap on a thumbnail with Not in your plan opens the plans screen.

SD and HD on device screens

SD is the lighter picture and HD the sharper one. Which of the two is used depends on the screen. The starting values come from Default quality in the settings.

ScreenStarting qualitySwitching on the screen
Thumbnails on the device pageMultiple cameras (SD unless changed); follows the setting at once.None.
Full-screen wallMultiple cameras.The SD/HD button switches all cameras. The change is not stored.
Live tabMultiple cameras.The SD/HD button in the top bar switches all cameras; see “SD and HD on a wall”.
Close-up in the full-screen wallSingle camera (HD unless changed).None.
Single-camera viewSingle camera.The SD/HD switch below the picture, when the device offers two streams. The change is not stored; see “Snapshot, sound and quality”.
LiveView Mix wallEach camera slot has its own choice, SD unless changed, set while the wall is arranged. The close-up of a camera on the wall always uses HD.See Chapter 8, “LiveView Mix”.
Recording playbackThe recorded stream is played. There is no choice between SD and HD.None.

Some devices provide only one stream for a channel. For those, SD and HD show the same picture, and the SD/HD switch of the single-camera view is not shown.

5The Live tab and the Full Screen Wall

The Live tab shows the enabled channels of one device as a wall of live pictures. On this tab the quality of the wall is switched, single cameras are opened, and the wall is extended to the Full Screen Wall. Cameras without a signal can be hidden from both walls.

The Live tab

Path: Live tab at the bottom of the screen.

The tab shows one device at a time: a recorder with all of its enabled channels, or one standalone camera. The title of the screen is the name of that device. To show cameras of different devices on one wall, use LiveView Mix; see Chapter 8, “LiveView Mix”.

  • Enabled channels only: channels that are disabled never appear on this tab. They are enabled on the device page; see “Channel options (long press)”.
  • Silent tiles: the tiles of a wall play no sound. Sound is available in the single-camera view; see “Snapshot, sound and quality”.
  • No refresh on this tab: the channel list of a device is read from the device when its device page opens; see “The device page”.
  • Leaving the app: when the app leaves the foreground, all streams stop. When the app returns, the tiles connect again.

Opening the Live tab

  1. Tap the Live tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the live pictures of the enabled channels of one device. The title is the name of the device. As long as no other device has been selected, the first device of the Devices tab is shown.

ControlPositionFunction
List button (Select Device)Top leftOpens the list of devices, in the order of the Devices tab. The device on the wall is marked.
SD or HDTop right, firstSwitches the quality of the whole wall at once (Switch all cameras to HD or Switch all cameras to SD). The text on the button is the current quality. See “SD and HD on a wall”.
Black-bar buttonTop right, secondCycles through Default, Enlarge to fill and Stretch to fill, as on the device page; see “The device page”. The change applies to this wall only and is not stored.
Full Screen WallTop right, thirdOpens the Full Screen Wall; see “The Full Screen Wall”.

While no device has been added, the SD/HD button and the Full Screen Wall button are unavailable. The black-bar button starts with the mode of Settings › Picture › Black bars. The Live tab reads that mode when the app starts, so a change in Settings reaches the Live tab at the next start of the app.

Showing another device

  1. Tap the list button (Select Device) in the top-left corner.

    Check: A menu lists all devices in the order of the Devices tab. The device that is shown is marked.

  2. Tap the name of the device.

    Check: The wall shows the enabled channels of the selected device, and the title changes to its name. The choice is stored and is still valid after the app has been closed.

The device for the Live tab can also be chosen in Open on launch; see “LiveView Mix in Settings”. When the selected device is deleted, the wall shows the first device of the list.

How the wall is arranged

ScreenPictures side by side
iPhone held upright1
iPhone held sideways2
iPad, in both orientations2

The tiles keep the 16:9 shape. When they do not fit on the screen, the wall scrolls vertically; the Live tab has no pages. The lower-left corner of each tile shows the number and the name of the channel. A device with only one enabled channel shows that camera over the whole area. Turning the device re-arranges the wall at once.

What a tile shows

TileMeaningTapping the tile
Live picture (a spinner while the connection is made)The channel is enabled, within the plan and online.Opens the single-camera view.
Failure message on a dark backgroundThe stream could not be opened. Cam Hub tries again by itself.Opens the single-camera view.
Grey, with a crossed-out camera and No signalThe device reports that the channel has no signal.Nothing happens.
Grey, with a pause symbol and PausedThe video of the channel was paused by hand on the device page; see “Channel options (long press)”. To resume it, use the device page.Opens the single-camera view.
Not in your plan with a lockThe channel is enabled, but the plan does not cover it; see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.Opens the plans screen.

Opening a camera

  1. Tap a tile that shows a live picture.

    Check: The single-camera view opens with the name of the camera as its title; see Chapter 6, “Single-camera view”. The back button returns to the Live tab.

  2. Tap a tile that shows Not in your plan.

    Check: The plans screen opens with a message at the top: Unlock every channel with an NVR plan. for a channel of a recorder, and You've reached the Free plan's limit of 2 enabled cameras. for a standalone camera. Close the screen with Done.

When the tab is empty

  • No device has been added: the screen shows No Devices and Add a device in the Devices tab first. See Chapter 3, “Adding a device”.
  • The device has no enabled channel, or every channel is hidden by Hide offline cameras: the screen shows No enabled cameras and Enable cameras on the device page. See “Choosing which cameras show”.

SD and HD on a wall

SD is the lighter picture and HD the sharper one. The button at the top of the Live tab and the button on the Full Screen Wall switch all cameras of the wall together.

  1. Tap the quality button at the top right of the Live tab (SD or HD).

    Check: The text on the button changes to the other quality, and the tiles connect again with the new quality.

  2. Tap the button again.

    Check: The wall returns to the first quality.

  • Starting quality: Settings › Default quality › Multiple cameras (SD unless changed). A change in Settings reaches the Live tab at once, until the button has been tapped on the Live tab; from then on the wall keeps that choice until the app is closed. The Full Screen Wall starts with the setting every time it opens.
  • Not stored: a quality chosen with the button is never saved.
  • One stream per channel: some devices provide only one stream for a channel. For those, SD and HD show the same picture.
  • Close-up: the close-up of a camera in the Full Screen Wall uses Single camera and has no switch; see “The full-screen wall of a device”.
  • For the quality on all other screens, see “SD and HD on device screens”; for the settings, see “Default quality”.

The Full Screen Wall

The Full Screen Wall shows all enabled channels of the device edge to edge on a black background. The status bar is hidden, and the picture reaches the edges of the screen as set by Edge-to-Edge Video; see “Picture: black bars and edge-to-edge”. The wall opens from the Live tab and from the device page; for the device page, see “The full-screen wall of a device”.

Opening the wall

  1. Tap the Full Screen Wall button (diagonal arrows) at the top right of the Live tab.

    Check: The wall covers the screen. At the top, the close button is on the left and the buttons for the quality, the layout and the black bars are on the right. When the device has no enabled channel, the screen shows No enabled cameras.

How the wall is arranged

ScreenArrangementMoving through the cameras
Held uprightThe tiles keep the 16:9 shape and are stacked in rows of two, or in rows of one after a tap on Layout.Scroll vertically. There are no pages and no dots.
Held sidewaysThe tiles are stretched so that the rows fill the height of the screen. On an iPhone with two tiles per row, a page holds four cameras; with one tile per row, one camera.Swipe sideways between pages. When there is more than one page, dots at the bottom show the current page.
One enabled channelThe camera fills the whole screen.None.

The same rule applies to an iPad: it follows the shape of the screen. Turning the device while the wall is open re-arranges the wall at once.

  1. Turn the iPhone sideways. Prerequisite: the rotation lock is off, and the device has more than four enabled channels.

    Check: The tiles fill the height of the screen, and the wall divides into pages. Dots at the bottom of the screen show the number of pages.

  2. Swipe to the left, then to the right.

    Check: The next page is shown, and then the previous page. The dots follow.

The buttons of the wall

ButtonFunctionStored
Close (top left)Closes the wall.No.
SD or HDSwitches the quality of all cameras at once; see “SD and HD on a wall”.No. The wall starts with Multiple cameras.

Black-bar buttonCycles through Default, Enlarge to fill and Stretch to fill.No. The wall starts with Black bars from Settings.

Changing the number of tiles per row

  1. Tap Layout at the top right of the wall.

    Check: The tiles are arranged one per row or two per row, and the symbol of the button changes. The next time the wall opens, it uses the same arrangement.

Opening a camera and closing the wall

  1. Tap a tile that shows a live picture.

    Check: A close-up of the camera opens over the wall, with Back and the name of the camera at the top. Its zoom, speaker, camera control and recordings are described in “The full-screen wall of a device”. The other cameras of the wall pause while the close-up is open. A tile with Not in your plan opens the plans screen, and a tile with No signal does nothing.

  2. Tap Close (the cross at the top left of the wall).

    Check: The Live tab is shown again.

Hiding cameras without signal

The setting Hide offline cameras removes cameras without a signal from the Live tab and from the Full Screen Wall. It is off by default. The device page still lists every channel and shows the channels without a signal in grey; see “What a thumbnail shows”. LiveView Mix walls are not affected: a slot without a signal keeps a plate with No signal.

  1. Tap the Settings tab, then scroll to Hide offline cameras. The row is in its own section below Picture.

    Check: The switch is off. The text below the row reads Cameras with no signal are hidden from the live walls. The device page still lists them, grayed out.

  2. Turn on Hide offline cameras.

    Check: The switch is on. All cameras are checked again.

  3. Tap the Live tab.

    Check: Cameras without a signal no longer appear on the wall. When no camera of the device remains, the screen shows No enabled cameras.

  • Which cameras are hidden: channels that the device reports as having no signal, and cameras whose stream could not be opened twice in a row. Cam Hub tries once more before a camera is hidden.
  • When a hidden camera returns: a hidden camera is not tried again until the app returns to the foreground, or until the switch is turned off and on again. The camera is then tried once more: it stays on the wall when it shows a picture, and it is hidden again when it fails again. A channel that the device reports as having no signal returns when the device reports a signal again; the report is updated when the device page reads the channel list.
  • Where it applies: to the Live tab and to the Full Screen Wall, including the Full Screen Wall of the device page. The setting is part of the backup of the app settings and is reset by Restore Default Settings; see “Reset: defaults, delete all data, delete iCloud backup”.

6Single-camera view

The single-camera view shows one camera at full width, live or from recordings. It offers zoom and pan, a snapshot, sound, the choice between SD and HD and, for cameras with a movable head, PTZ control. For devices that support playback, the view also holds the recording timeline; see Chapter 7, “Recording playback and speed”.

Opening the view

The view opens from three places:

  • the Devices tab: a thumbnail on the device page (see “The device page”);
  • the Live tab: a thumbnail on the wall (see “The Live tab”);
  • the close-up of a camera on a full-screen wall or on a LiveView Mix wall: the Recordings button (see “The full-screen wall of a device”).

Prerequisite: the channel is enabled, within the plan and online. On the device page, a paused channel does not open the view either; see “What a thumbnail shows”.

  1. Tap the Devices tab, then tap the device.

    Check: The device page shows the thumbnails of the channels.

  2. Tap the thumbnail of a channel that shows a live picture.

    Check: The single-camera view opens. The title is the name of the camera, and the green badge LIVE is shown at the top left of the picture. The picture starts with the quality of Settings › Default quality › Single camera (HD unless changed).

Tap the back button in the top-left corner to leave the view.

The parts of the screen

PartContent
Picture (upright, 16:9)The badge at the top left names the mode: LIVE (green) or PLAYBACK 15:00:03, with the playback time (red). The round button at the lower right is the camera control for PTZ in live mode; see “PTZ control: moving the camera”. While a recording plays, it is the speed button; see “Playback speed”.
Controls barSnapshot at the left, the speaker button next to it when the camera sends sound, and at the right the SD/HD switch in live mode or Back to Live during playback; see “Snapshot, sound and quality”.
Recording panelThe heading Recordings with the day, the timeline and the list of recordings. The panel appears only for devices that support playback; for all other devices, the view consists of the picture and the controls bar. See Chapter 7, “Recording playback and speed”.

While a picture is shown, the screen of the iPhone or iPad does not dim.

Zoom and pan

The picture can be enlarged on the screen. This is a digital enlargement of the picture and works in live mode and during playback. It does not move the lens of the camera; for that, see “PTZ control: moving the camera”.

GestureEffect
Spread two fingers apart on the pictureEnlarges the picture up to 6 times. Moving the fingers together reduces it again; below normal size, the picture returns to normal size.
Drag one finger while the picture is enlargedMoves the picture. The edge of the picture never leaves a gap.
Double-tap the pictureEnlarges the picture to 2.5 times. When the picture is already enlarged, it returns to normal size.

  1. Spread two fingers apart on the picture.

    Check: The picture is enlarged. The badge at the top left keeps its place.

  2. Drag one finger across the picture.

    Check: The picture moves in the direction of the finger.

  3. Double-tap the picture.

    Check: The picture returns to normal size.

Snapshot, sound and quality

Taking a snapshot

  1. Tap Snapshot at the left of the controls bar.

    Check: The sheet Snapshot slides up. It shows a progress indicator and then the picture.

  2. Tap Share.

    Check: The sharing sheet of the system opens. From there, the picture can be saved, copied or sent with the actions that the system offers.

  3. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The sheet closes.

  • The snapshot is a current picture that Cam Hub requests from the device. It is taken from the live picture of the device also while a recording plays, and it is not a frame of the recording.
  • When the device cannot supply a snapshot, for example a device that was added through a brand from the list, the sheet closes again without a message.

Switching the sound on and off

The speaker button appears only when the camera sends sound in a format that Cam Hub can play. A camera without sound, or with an unsupported sound format, has no button.

  1. Tap the speaker button next to Snapshot (Unmute).

    Check: The symbol changes from a crossed-out speaker to a speaker with sound waves, and the sound of the camera plays.

  2. Tap the speaker button again (Mute).

    Check: The symbol shows the crossed-out speaker again, and the sound stops.

  • Cam Hub only plays the sound of the camera. There is no microphone and no two-way talk.
  • The sound plays even when the ring/silent switch of the iPhone is set to silent.
  • The choice is one switch for the whole app. It is remembered and is off at first. Thumbnails and walls never play sound; only the single-camera view and the close-up of a camera do.
  • While camera sound plays, other audio on the iPhone is lowered. Sound stops when the app leaves the foreground.
  • During playback, sound plays at normal speed only; see “Playback speed”.

Switching between SD and HD

  1. Tap SD or HD in the switch at the right of the controls bar.

    Check: The stream restarts, Connecting… shows briefly, and the picture continues with the selected quality. The change is not stored.

The switch is shown only in live mode and only when the device offers two streams for the camera. During playback, Back to Live takes its place. The starting quality comes from Settings › Default quality › Single camera. HD is sharper and uses more bandwidth and more resources of the iPhone. For devices that provide one stream per channel, SD and HD are the same picture. The rules for all screens are in “SD and HD on device screens”.

Black bars, rotation and landscape

  • Black bars: the picture follows Settings › Picture › Black bars (Default, Enlarge to fill or Stretch to fill; see “The device page”). The single-camera view has no switch of its own; a change in Settings applies to this view as well.
  • Edge-to-Edge Video: in landscape, the picture extends into the area of the Dynamic Island and the rounded corners when Settings › Picture › Edge-to-Edge Video is on. When the setting is off, the picture stays clear of them, with black bars.
  • iPad: the layout does not change with the orientation. The view keeps the arrangement of the upright iPhone in both orientations, and the picture-only landscape layout below is not used.

Watching in landscape on an iPhone

Prerequisite: the rotation lock of the iPhone is off.

  1. Turn the iPhone sideways.

    Check: The picture fills the whole screen. The navigation bar, the tab bar, the status bar, the controls bar and the recording panel are hidden. The back button and the other buttons of the picture show for about 5 seconds and then fade out.

  2. Tap the picture once.

    Check: The back button appears at the top left, the speaker button at the top right when the camera sends sound, and the camera control button at the lower right when the camera can be moved. The buttons fade out again after about 5 seconds; another tap on the picture shows them again.

  3. Tap the back button at the top left, or turn the iPhone upright again.

    Check: The view leaves the landscape layout or closes. The back button returns to the page from which the view was opened.

Zoom, pan and PTZ control work in landscape as in upright orientation. Snapshot, the SD/HD switch, the day and the list of recordings are available in upright orientation only. For the strip that appears in landscape during playback, see “Playback in landscape”.

PTZ control: moving the camera

Prerequisites: a camera with a movable head (pan, tilt or zoom), a device that supports PTZ control, an account that may control PTZ on the device, and live mode. During playback, the camera control is hidden.

Cam Hub asks the device for the abilities of the channel when the view opens. The round button at the lower right of the picture appears when the answer arrives, which can take a moment. A camera that cannot move shows no button. Only the controls that the device reports are shown.

  1. Tap the round button at the lower right of the picture (Move camera).

    Check: The pad opens to the left of the button, and the button shows a cross (Hide camera controls). The pad holds a capsule with plus and minus for zoom, a disc with four arrows and a house symbol in the middle, and a star button.

  2. Press and hold an arrow of the disc (Tilt up, Tilt down, Pan left or Pan right).

    Check: The camera turns in that direction for as long as the finger stays on the arrow, and the picture follows. The camera stops when the finger is lifted.

  3. Press and hold plus or minus on the capsule (Zoom in or Zoom out).

    Check: The lens of the camera zooms in or out for as long as the finger stays, and stops when the finger is lifted.

  4. Tap the house symbol (Home position).

    Check: The camera moves to its home position.

  5. Tap the star button (Saved positions).

    Check: A dialog lists the names of the positions that are stored in the camera. When the camera has none, the dialog shows This camera has no saved positions.

  6. Tap the name of a position.

    Check: The camera moves to that position, and the list closes. Tap outside the list to close it without moving the camera.

  7. Tap the cross button (Hide camera controls).

    Check: The pad closes, and a movement that is still running stops.

ControlShown when the device reports
Direction disc with four arrowsThe head can pan or tilt. The house symbol sits in the middle of the disc.
Capsule with plus and minusThe head can zoom.
Star buttonThe camera has saved positions.
House symbol next to the starThe head can go to its home position but cannot pan or tilt; the disc is not shown then.
  • Speed: the app has no speed setting. A button moves the camera at one fixed speed, the highest that the app requests, for as long as it is held; a short tap makes a short movement.
  • Refused movements: when the device refuses a movement, no message is shown.
  • Saved positions: Cam Hub recalls positions that exist on the camera. Positions are created and changed on the device itself, not in Cam Hub.
  • Stopping: a movement stops when the finger is lifted, when the view is left, when the app leaves the foreground, when the pad is closed and when playback starts. The same pad is available in the close-up of a camera on full-screen walls and on LiveView Mix walls.

Connection states and messages

The state of the stream is shown over the picture.

Over the pictureMeaning and action
Spinner with Connecting…The first connection is being made.
Spinner with Reconnecting…The stream was interrupted. Cam Hub tries again by itself at growing intervals of up to about 15 seconds and continues until the view is left.
Message with a warning symbol and RetryThe stream could not be opened. The message names the cause, for example an unreachable device or a refused account; the wording is the same as when a device is added (see “When adding fails: the checklist”). Tap Retry to try again.
Too many requests just now. Try again in a minute. with RetryToo many requests reached the device or its service in a short time. Cam Hub does not try again by itself in this case. Wait a minute, then tap Retry.
Could not load the saved password for this device. with RetryThe saved password cannot be read. Add the device again with the same address, HTTP port and user name to store the password again; see “The Add Device form”.
Locked — upgrade to enable with PlansThe channel is outside the plan, for example because the plan ended while the view was open. Tap Plans to open the plans screen, or free a place as described in “Plan limits and enabling channels”.
End of recording with Back to LiveThe recording that was playing has no continuation; see “While a recording plays”.
No recording at the selected time. with RetryNo recording exists at the time that was chosen on the timeline; see “Using the timeline”.

  1. Read the message over the picture.

    Check: The message names the cause.

  2. Tap Retry.

    Check: The spinner Connecting… appears. The picture follows, or the message appears again; in that case, work through the checks in “When adding fails: the checklist” and Chapter 15, “Troubleshooting”.

Messages that come from the stream itself can be shown in English whatever the language of the app, for example Wrong username or password, Connection closed or HTTP 404.

A picture that stays black without a message can mean that the device sends a video format that the iPhone cannot decode. Cam Hub plays H.264 and H.265 video only, and a picture size beyond the limit of the decoder of the iPhone is not displayed. A lower resolution or the H.264 format in the settings of the device can help.

When the app moves to the background or the iPhone is locked, the stream stops. When the app returns, the stream connects again by itself. A recording that was playing resumes where it had reached.

What is not available

  • Switching to the next or previous camera by swiping. Each camera is opened from its thumbnail.
  • A button for full screen. Turning the iPhone sideways takes its place.
  • A microphone and two-way talk. The app plays the sound of the camera only.
  • Controls for focus, iris and PTZ speed, and storing or changing saved positions.
  • A snapshot for devices that cannot supply one, and saving or sharing recordings; see “What is not available”.

7Recording playback and speed

For devices that support playback, the single-camera view switches from the live picture to recorded footage. A day is chosen, a 24-hour timeline is moved to the wanted time, and a recording or a detected person is played from the list. A recording can be played faster at 2×, 4× or 8×.

Where playback is available

The recording panel appears below the picture of the single-camera view (see Chapter 6, “Single-camera view”) only for devices that support playback. For all other devices, the view shows the live picture and the controls bar only. Playback is reached from three places: the single-camera view itself, the Recordings button in the close-up of a camera on a full-screen wall (see “The full-screen wall of a device”), and the same button on a LiveView Mix wall.

OfferShown when
Recording panel with day, timeline and listThe device supports playback and the account may read recordings on it.
Switch Continuous and EventsThe device also keeps an index of detected people. Without the index, only the list of continuous recordings is shown, with no switch.
Speed buttonDuring playback, when the device can play the recording faster. If it cannot, a notice appears; see “Playback speed”.
  • Recorder channel: the recordings of the channel come from the storage of the recorder. The single-camera view of a channel shows the recordings of that channel only.
  • Standalone camera: the recordings come from the storage of the camera itself, for cameras that offer a search for recordings. A camera without recordings shows an empty day.
  • The screen and the controls are the same for both. A recorder and a camera differ only in where the recordings are kept and in whether the device supports playback.
  • A device that was added through ONVIF supports playback only when it offers the ONVIF services for searching and replaying recordings. Otherwise, the day shows an empty list.
  • A device that was added through a brand from the list provides live view only, without playback; see “Choosing the connection method”. The sample cameras contain no recordings.

Choosing a day

Prerequisite: the single-camera view of a camera that supports playback is open; see “Opening the view”. Below the controls bar, the heading Recordings shows the current day on its right, with the timeline below it and the list of recordings below the timeline.

  1. Tap the day on the right of the heading Recordings.

    Check: A calendar opens.

  2. Tap the wanted day.

    Check: The calendar closes, and the heading shows the new day. Loading recordings… appears briefly, then the timeline and the list show the recordings of that day. The picture does not change.

  • The cursor of the timeline starts at the current time of the device for today, and at 12:00 for any other day.
  • Choosing a day does not start playback by itself. Playback starts from the timeline or from the list.
  • The timeline shows the chosen day and the day before it, so that footage across midnight can be reached.
  • Any day can be chosen, including days without recordings. Such a day shows an empty list.

Using the timeline

The timeline shows the recordings of the chosen day along a ruler. The orange cursor stays in the middle, and the ruler moves under it. All times are the clock of the device, not the time zone of the iPhone.

ElementMeaning
Orange line with a bubble above itThe cursor, fixed in the middle. The bubble shows the time at the cursor, and the date as well while the cursor is on the day before the chosen day.
Blue barsContinuous recordings.
Red barsRecordings that the device made because of an event.
Thin red marksDetected people, for devices that keep a detection index.
Dark gapsNo recording exists at that time.
Dimmed part at the left, with a dashed line and a dateThe day before the chosen day. A dashed line with a date marks every midnight.
Hour labels below the barThe scale. The divisions become finer when the timeline is enlarged.
Two magnifier buttons at the rightZoom in (plus) and Zoom out (minus) change the span that the timeline shows.

  1. Touch the timeline and drag sideways.

    Check: The ruler moves under the cursor, and the time in the bubble changes. The picture stays live while the finger moves.

  2. Lift the finger when the cursor is at the wanted time.

    Check: The picture switches to the recording from that time. The badge turns red and shows PLAYBACK 15:00:03 with the time of the playback, and Back to Live replaces the SD/HD switch.

  3. Tap Zoom in (the plus magnifier), or spread two fingers apart on the timeline.

    Check: The timeline shows a shorter span, down to 10 minutes. The button is dimmed at that limit.

  4. Tap Zoom out (the minus magnifier), or bring two fingers together on the timeline.

    Check: The timeline shows a longer span, up to 48 hours (both days). The button is dimmed at that limit. The timeline opens with a span of 24 hours.

  • A drag shorter than about 6 points on the screen is ignored, so that touching the timeline does not leave the live picture by accident.
  • When the finger is lifted in a gap, the next recording after the gap plays. The badge and the cursor jump to the start of that recording. When no recording follows, the message No recording at the selected time. appears with Retry.
  • While a recording plays, the cursor follows the playback by itself. While the timeline is being touched, the cursor stays where the finger puts it.

The list of recordings and the search for people

Below the timeline, a list shows the recordings of the chosen day. When the device keeps a detection index, a switch above the list selects Continuous or Events.

  • Continuous: one row per continuous recording, newest first. Each row shows a blue dot, the start time and the length of the recording in hours, minutes and seconds. A row of the day before starts with the date. The row of the recording that is playing is highlighted and shows a speaker symbol.
  • Events: one row Person detected per detection, newest first, with the start time. Detections that follow each other within 2 seconds are merged into one row.

Playing a recording from the list

  1. Tap a row under Continuous.

    Check: The picture switches to that recording, from its start. The row is highlighted, and the cursor jumps to the start time.

Finding a person

  1. Tap Events above the list.

    Check: The list shows the rows Person detected. The timeline shows the detections as thin red marks.

  2. Tap a row.

    Check: Playback starts about 5 seconds before the detection, or at the start of the recording when the recording began later. The badge shows the playback time.

Only people are searched. Recordings that were triggered by other events appear as red bars on the timeline and are played by moving the timeline to them. Cam Hub reads at most about 400 recordings and 2,000 detections per channel and day; anything beyond that is not listed.

MessageMeaning
Loading recordings…The device is being searched for the day.
No continuous recordings on this day.The day has no continuous recording.
No people detected on this day.The day has no detection.
This device could not search its person-event index.Shown under Events when the device does not answer the search for people. The continuous list is not affected.
Message with a warning symbol above the timeline: This account cannot read recordings on this device., Could not reach the device., The device did not recognize this camera's recordings. or This camera is offline.The search for the day failed for the reason that the message names. The day can be changed, and another day tried, while the message is shown. For the account, check its rights on the device; for the connection, see Chapter 15, “Troubleshooting”.
Too many requests just now. Try again in a minute.The device or its service refused the search because of too many requests. Wait a minute and choose the day again.
Other messages in the same place, for example The device sent an unexpected reply., The connection timed out. or Something went wrong. Please try again.The search failed for another reason. Choose the day again. When the message persists, see Chapter 15, “Troubleshooting”.

While a recording plays

  • Badge: the red badge at the top left of the picture shows the playback time on the clock of the device, and the time moves with the picture. It matches the time that the camera prints into its picture, when the camera does so. When the playback time is on the day before the chosen day, the date precedes the time.
  • Continuing: when a recording file ends, playback continues into the next recording by itself, so that an evening can be watched without a stop at every file. Cam Hub looks for newer recordings first, because the device may still be writing.
  • Sound: the speaker button works at normal speed only; see “Snapshot, sound and quality”.
  • Snapshot: takes the current live picture of the device, not a frame of the recording.
  • Zoom and pan: work as in live mode; see “Zoom and pan”. The camera control for PTZ is hidden during playback.
  • Recordings that arrive as a file: some devices deliver a recording as a file. The picture area then shows Downloading recording… 45% with a progress bar, and the recording plays in the video player of the system, which has its own controls. The timeline cursor does not follow in that case. The downloaded files are kept in a cache of up to 500 MB on the iPhone, so that the same recording does not have to be downloaded again; Delete All Data removes the cache.
  • Background: when the app leaves the foreground or the iPhone is locked, playback stops. When the app returns, playback resumes at the point it had reached.

Returning to the live picture

  1. Tap Back to Live in the controls bar.

    Check: The live picture returns with the quality that was used before. The badge shows LIVE, the day changes to today, the cursor moves to the current time, and the speed returns to 1×.

At the end of the last recording

When the playback passes the end of the last recording, the last picture stays on the screen, and a card with End of recording and Back to Live appears. This is not an error.

  1. Tap Back to Live on the card.

    Check: The live picture returns as described above.

Playback speed

The speed button is a round button at the lower right of the picture. It shows the current speed, 1× at normal speed. Each tap selects the next of four speeds, in the order 1×, 2×, 4×, 8× and back to 1×. The button is shown only during playback and only when the recording can be played faster; it appears a moment after the recording starts. Live pictures always run at normal speed.

  1. Start a recording, as described in “Using the timeline” or “The list of recordings and the search for people”.

    Check: The speed button at the lower right of the picture shows 1×.

  2. Tap the speed button.

    Check: The button shows 2× and is tinted. The picture reopens at the current position, and the time advances twice as fast. About one second of the picture is lost when the stream reopens.

  3. Tap the speed button again.

    Check: The button shows 4×, and the time advances four times as fast.

  4. Tap the speed button again.

    Check: The button shows 8×, and the time advances eight times as fast.

  5. Tap the speed button again.

    Check: The button shows 1×, and the recording plays at normal speed.

  • The speed stays selected when another recording or another time is chosen during the same playback. Back to Live returns it to 1×.
  • Sound plays at 1× only. Above 1×, the picture runs without sound.
  • A higher speed makes the device send the picture faster, which uses more bandwidth.
  • The button is not shown for devices that stream recordings in a way that does not allow a change of speed.
  • In landscape orientation, the speed button is part of the strip over the picture; see “Playback in landscape”. The notice for a device that cannot play faster is not shown there; the button only returns to 1×.
A device that cannot play faster

Not every device accepts a faster speed. When the device cannot play the recording faster, the notice This recorder can't play faster than normal speed. appears above the button for about 4 seconds, and the button returns to 1×. The notice can take a few seconds to appear, because Cam Hub tries several ways of requesting the faster speed before it gives up. The same happens when the device accepts the request but the picture does not run faster. The recording continues at normal speed.

Playback in landscape

Prerequisite: the rotation lock of the iPhone is off. On an iPad, the layout does not change with the orientation; the steps below apply to the iPhone.
