  1. Start a recording and turn the iPhone sideways.

    Check: The picture fills the screen. A strip over the lower edge of the picture holds the badge PLAYBACK 15:00:03, the speed button, Back to Live and the timeline.

  2. Drag the timeline in the strip and lift the finger at the wanted time.

    Check: The picture plays the recording from that time, as in upright orientation.

  3. Leave the strip untouched for about 5 seconds.

    Check: The strip and the buttons at the top of the picture fade out. A tap on the picture shows them again.

  4. Tap Back to Live in the strip, or turn the iPhone upright again.

    Check: The live picture returns, or the upright layout with the recording panel is shown again.

The strip appears only during playback, because a live picture has nothing to scrub. The day, the list of recordings, Snapshot and the SD/HD switch are available in upright orientation only.

What is not available

  • Playback for devices that were added through a brand from the list, and for the sample cameras; see “Where playback is available”.
  • A search for events other than people.
  • A timeline that spans more than the chosen day and the day before it.
  • Saving, exporting or deleting recordings. Recordings can be watched only; a snapshot always shows the current live picture.
  • A choice between SD and HD during playback, slow motion, reverse playback, and speeds other than 1×, 2×, 4× and 8×.
  • Sound at speeds above 1×.
  • A pause button, frame-by-frame stepping, jumps of a few seconds, a box for entering a time, buttons for the next or previous recording, and a free-text search.
  • Playback on Apple TV is described in Chapter 14, “Apple TV”.

8LiveView Mix

LiveView Mix places cameras from different devices on one wall. The wall can also hold pictures, clocks, labels and control panels. This chapter follows the order of the work: the tab and its preview, choosing cameras, layouts, arranging, the full-screen wall, and the effect of plan limits on the wall.

Terms used in this chapter

Slot: one position on the wall. Slots are filled with cameras in order; an empty slot can hold a picture, a clock, a label or a control panel instead.

Layout: the arrangement of the tiles on the screen, for example 2 × 3 or 1 + 5.

Page: the tiles that a layout shows at once. When there are more slots than the layout holds, the full-screen wall is divided into pages.

The LiveView Mix tab and its preview

Location: the LiveView Mix tab, the leftmost tab at the bottom of the screen. Before setup, the screen shows an explanation and the Set Up LiveView Mix button; for the procedure, see “Building a first wall of six cameras”. Once the wall holds at least one slot with content (a camera, a picture, a control panel, a clock or a label), the tab shows the preview, with the note Preview only — full screen shows your layout. below it.

Three buttons in the top-right corner are, from left to right:

ButtonPurposeDetails
Full screen (diagonal arrows icon)Opens the wall in the selected layout.“The full-screen wall”
Choose Cameras (camera icon)Selects the cameras on the wall and their quality.“Choosing cameras and quality”
Adjust the Layout (grid icon)Selects the layout, the black-bar handling, the watermark and paging, and opens the arrangement.“Adjusting the layout”

The preview behaves as follows:

  • The preview shows all slots in order in an even grid. It does not take the shape of the selected layout; the layout takes effect on the full-screen wall only.
  • The preview uses the SD or HD setting of each camera, the black-bar setting of the wall and the watermark.
  • On an iPhone held upright, the preview has two columns, and the number of rows depends on the height of the screen. Held sideways, the preview adds columns (typically four) so that two rows fill the screen. On an iPad, the preview normally keeps two columns. When there are more slots than fit, swipe left or right to change the page; page dots appear below the preview.
  • When the wall has only one slot, that slot fills the whole preview area.
  • While the watermark is off, each camera shows its channel number and name in the bottom-left corner. When the watermark is on, the watermark replaces this label.
  • Tapping a camera picture opens the full-screen viewer; see “Opening a single camera”. Tapping a button of a control panel sends its request; when the button is set to ask for confirmation first, a confirmation dialog appears; see Chapter 9, “Control panels and webhooks”.
  • A camera that cannot be shown keeps its slot and shows a status text; see “When a slot cannot show a camera”.
  • While the full-screen wall is open, the preview pauses its streams; they resume when the tab is shown again.
  • When no slot has anything to show (for example when every slot points at a camera that has been removed), the screen shows LiveView Mix is empty with a pointer to Settings.
Hold the device sideways

The layouts are drawn for a wide screen. Held sideways, the tiles keep the wide shape of camera pictures; held upright, the layout is flipped about its diagonal (see “Black bars, edge-to-edge video and the angle of the device”). The preview and the full-screen wall rearrange themselves with the angle of the device. No setting is needed.

Building a first wall of six cameras

Purpose: place six cameras on one wall and view it full screen in the 1 + 5 layout. Time needed: about 5 minutes.

Prerequisites:

  • The devices have been added and offer at least six channels to choose from; for adding, see Chapter 3, “Adding a device”.
  • All six channels are enabled and within the allowance of the plan. The Free plan allows only 2 enabled channels across the whole app; channels beyond that appear on the wall as Disabled or Not in your plan. For the allowances and for enabling channels, see “How plan limits affect the wall” and Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.
  • The device is an iPhone or an iPad. For Apple TV, see “Differences on Apple TV”.

  1. Tap the LiveView Mix tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: When LiveView Mix has not been set up, the screen shows an explanation and the Set Up LiveView Mix button.

  2. Tap Set Up LiveView Mix.

    Check: The Choose Cameras page opens and lists all channels, grouped by device. The top of the page shows 0 cameras selected.

  3. Tap the circle in front of the first of the six channels.

    Check: The circle is ticked, and an SD and HD selector appears on the right of the row, set to SD.

  4. Tick five more channels, in the order in which they should appear on the wall.

    Check: The top of the page shows 6 cameras selected.

  5. Optional: tap HD beside each camera that should show a sharper picture.

    Check: The selector of that camera shows HD. The other cameras are unchanged.

  6. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes and the tab shows a preview of the six cameras.

  7. Tap Adjust the Layout (the grid icon) in the top-right corner.

    Check: The Adjust the Layout page opens. The top of the page shows This layout holds 4 · 6 placed. The default layout holds only 4 tiles per page, so six cameras would use two pages.

  8. In the Full-screen layout section, tap 1 + 5.

    Check: The layout is highlighted, and the top of the page shows This layout holds 6 · 6 placed.

  9. Scroll down to the Watermark section and switch on Show watermark.

    Check: The section shows the options for position, content and style. Device name and Camera name are on.

  10. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes. Every camera in the preview is marked with its device name and camera name.

  11. Turn the device sideways.

    Check: The preview rearranges itself for the new angle. No setting is needed.

  12. Tap Full screen (the diagonal arrows icon) in the top-right corner.

    Check: The wall fills the screen: the first camera is in the large tile in the top-left corner (two thirds of the width and height), and the other five are to its right and below it. A ✕ button is in the top-left corner.

  13. Tap the picture of any camera.

    Check: The screen changes to the single-camera view of that camera, playing in HD, with a back button in the top-left corner.

  14. Tap the back button ‹ in the top-left corner.

    Check: The screen shows the full-screen wall again.

  15. Tap ✕ in the top-left corner.

    Check: The wall closes and the preview in the LiveView Mix tab is shown again.

Expected outcome: the LiveView Mix tab shows a preview of six cameras, and the full-screen wall shows them in the 1 + 5 layout, with the first camera in the large tile. To put a different camera in the large tile, see “Arranging the wall and its slots”. When some tiles show a status text instead of a picture, see “When a slot cannot show a camera” and Chapter 15, “Troubleshooting”.

Choosing cameras and quality

Path: LiveView Mix › Choose Cameras. The page can also be opened from Settings › LiveView Mix, where the camera selection and the layout options are on one page; see “LiveView Mix in Settings”.

ItemDescription
Count at the top of the page6 cameras selected updates as channels are ticked. It counts cameras only, not empty slots, pictures, clocks, labels or control panels.
Channel rowsOne section per device and one row per channel: a circle, a thumbnail, the channel number and the name. The thumbnail shows a live picture only for channels that the plan covers; the others show Disabled or Not in your plan.
Order of tickingThe order in which channels are ticked is the order in which they fill the wall. A newly ticked camera goes last.
DuplicatesA channel can be placed on the wall only once.
SD | HDAfter a channel is ticked, a quality selector appears on the right of its row. A newly added camera is set to SD.
All SD, All HDTwo buttons at the top of the page that set the quality of all selected cameras at once.
No DevicesShown when no device has been added yet, with a prompt to add one first.

The quality rule of LiveView Mix

  • LiveView Mix has its own quality, set for each slot. It is not affected by Single camera and Multiple cameras under Settings › Default quality; those settings apply to the single-camera view and to the ordinary device walls only.
  • Each tile on the wall plays in SD or HD according to its own setting. When tiles are small, HD and SD look almost the same. Using SD for most tiles and HD only for the cameras that need to be seen clearly reduces the load on bandwidth and on the device.
  • A single camera that is opened from the wall or from the preview always starts in HD, whatever the setting of its slot. In the full-screen viewer of the preview, the quality can be switched for the current viewing; the switch is not saved. See “Opening a single camera”.
  • The thumbnails on the Choose Cameras page and on the arrange canvas always use SD.

To choose cameras:

  1. In the LiveView Mix tab, tap Choose Cameras (the camera icon).

    Check: The Choose Cameras page opens. Cameras that are already selected are ticked.

  2. Tap the circle in front of a channel to add it to the wall.

    Check: The circle is ticked, SD and HD appear on the row, and the count at the top increases by 1.

  3. To change the quality of that camera, tap HD or SD.

    Check: The selector shows the chosen quality. Only this camera is affected.

  4. Optional: to change the quality of all selected cameras at once, tap All SD or All HD.

    Check: The selectors of all selected cameras show the same quality.

  5. To remove a camera from the wall, tap the circle of a ticked channel again.

    Check: The circle is empty again, and the count at the top decreases by 1.

  6. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes and the preview is updated to the new selection.

Unticking a camera moves the following slots forward

After a camera is unticked, every slot behind it moves forward by one, including empty slots, pictures, clocks, labels and control panels. To keep a gap, use an empty slot in Arrange the wall instead; see “Arranging the wall and its slots”.

When the page is opened with the button in the top-right corner of the LiveView Mix tab, Cancel in the top-left corner restores the wall to its state before the page was opened. Done keeps the selection.

Slots that point at removed cameras

When a slot on the wall points at a camera that Cam Hub no longer has, the top of the Choose Cameras page shows 2 slots point at cameras that were removed. and the Empty Those Slots button. These slots do not appear in the list of ticks.

  1. Tap Empty Those Slots.

    Check: The note and the button disappear. These slots become empty slots in place, and all other cameras keep their positions.

Adjusting the layout

Path: LiveView Mix › Adjust the Layout. The top of the page shows This layout holds 6 · 6 placed: the first number is the number of tiles per page of the selected layout, the second is the number of slots on the wall that hold content. Placed slots include cameras and also configured pictures, control panels, clocks and labels, but not empty slots that are left blank on purpose.

The Full-screen layout section lists the ready-made layouts in order, with Custom last. Each layout is shown as a small diagram of its shape, with its name below.

LayoutTiles per pageShape
2 × 242 columns, 2 rows, tiles of equal size
2 × 362 columns, 3 rows, tiles of equal size
3 × 393 columns, 3 rows, tiles of equal size
3 × 4123 columns, 4 rows, tiles of equal size
4 × 4164 columns, 4 rows, tiles of equal size
1 + 34One large tile on the left (two thirds of the width) and three small tiles in a column on the right
1 + 56One large tile in the top-left corner (two thirds of the width and height) and five small tiles to its right and below it
1 + 78One large tile in the top-left corner (three quarters of the width and height) and seven small tiles to its right and below it
CustomUp to 64A layout drawn by hand; see “Drawing a custom layout”
  • Slots fill the tiles in the order of the layout. The first camera goes into the first tile; in a layout with one large tile, the first tile is the large one.
  • When a page cannot hold all slots, the remaining slots go to the next page. For example, 6 slots in the 2 × 2 layout use 2 pages: 4 tiles on the first page and 2 on the second, with the remaining positions black.
  • A layout with more than 16 tiles carries a TV icon (Best on a large screen) in the top-right corner of its diagram. It is hard to read on a phone and is better viewed on an iPad or an Apple TV.
  • On an iPhone and an iPad, the ready-made layouts offered are those with up to 16 tiles. Ready-made layouts with more than 16 tiles (5 × 4 to 7 × 7, 1 + 21 and 1 + 27) are offered only on Apple TV; see Chapter 14, “Apple TV”. A wall that is already set to one of them (for example after a restore) is still shown correctly, and its diagram appears in the list. To place more slots on a phone or an iPad, use a custom layout.
  • The Custom diagram shows the layout that was drawn. Until one has been drawn, it shows the starting shape; tapping it selects that shape.

To select a layout:

  1. In the LiveView Mix tab, tap Adjust the Layout (the grid icon).

    Check: The Adjust the Layout page opens. The layout in use is highlighted.

  2. In the Full-screen layout section, tap the layout to use.

    Check: The selected layout is highlighted, and the number of tiles per page at the top is updated.

  3. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes. The preview keeps its even grid, and the selected layout takes effect on the full-screen wall.

The same page also holds the arrangement, the black bars, the watermark and the paging option, described in “Arranging the wall and its slots”, “Black bars, edge-to-edge video and the angle of the device”, “Watermark” and “LiveView Mix in Settings” respectively.

The scope of Cancel and Done

The Choose Cameras and Adjust the Layout pages that open from the LiveView Mix tab each have Cancel and Done. Cancel restores the wall to its state before the page was opened, including any arrangement or custom layout made inside it. Custom layout, Arrange and Slot N each have their own Cancel and Done: Done only returns to the previous level, and Cancel restores only what was changed since that level was entered. To keep all changes, tap Done all the way back to the outermost page.

Drawing a custom layout

Path: LiveView Mix › Adjust the Layout › Draw a custom layout. When none of the ready-made layouts fits, the number of rows and columns of the grid can be chosen freely, and neighboring cells can be merged into larger tiles.

ItemDescription
Starting shapeA 3 × 3 grid whose top-left 2 × 2 block is already merged into one large tile: 6 tiles in all.
Rows, ColumnsSet with − and +, from 2 to 8. The maximum is 8 × 8, which is 64 tiles.
TilesThe total number of tiles after merging. With more than 16 tiles, a note appears below: That many tiles is best viewed on iPad or Apple TV.
MergingDrag a finger across several cells of the grid; the rectangle that is covered becomes one large tile. A large tile can only be a rectangle, not an L shape or any other irregular shape.
SplittingTap a merged tile to split it back into single cells. Tapping a single cell does nothing.
Split every blockSplits all large tiles at once. The button is unavailable when there are none.
NumbersThe number on each tile follows reading order (left to right, top to bottom) and is the order in which cameras fill the tiles. A large tile takes the position of its top-left cell.
Use this layoutMakes the drawn layout the layout of the wall. When it is already in use, the button is replaced by Your wall is using this layout.

  1. In the LiveView Mix tab, tap Adjust the Layout.

    Check: The Adjust the Layout page opens.

  2. In the Full-screen layout section, tap Draw a custom layout.

    Check: The Custom layout page opens: the grid is at the top, with Rows, Columns and Tiles below it.

  3. Set the size of the grid with − and + on the right of Rows and Columns.

    Check: The grid is redrawn with the new number of rows and columns, and Tiles is updated. When rows or columns are reduced, any large tile that no longer fits is removed.

  4. Drag one finger across the grid, from the first cell to be merged to the last.

    Check: During the drag, the covered area is highlighted. After the finger is lifted, the cells in that area are merged into one large tile, Tiles decreases and the numbers are reassigned.

  5. To split a large tile, tap it once.

    Check: The large tile is split into single cells, and Tiles increases.

  6. Tap Use this layout.

    Check: The button is replaced by Your wall is using this layout.

  7. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The screen returns to the Adjust the Layout page. The Custom diagram is selected and shows the shape that was drawn last.

  • When a drag touches existing large tiles, those tiles are split first, and then only the dragged rectangle is merged. The area is never enlarged automatically.
  • When a drag goes beyond the edge of the grid, the area stops at the cells on the edge.
  • Every change to the grid and the large tiles is stored immediately. Tapping Cancel in the top-left corner restores everything that was changed since the page was opened.
  • Drawing a layout without tapping Use this layout does not change the current wall; a shape that is not in use can also be tidied up here.
  • The drawn layout is kept even when a ready-made layout is selected for a while. Tapping the Custom diagram later returns to that shape.
  • The custom layout can also be selected in the layout row at the top of the Arrange page, but its shape can only be edited here.

Special layouts: big and small tiles on one wall

A custom layout can merge neighboring cells into large tiles. This makes a layout like the video wall of a monitoring center: the important cameras are enlarged, the others are reduced to small tiles, and clocks, labels or control panels share the same wall.

Example: a grid of 4 rows and 4 columns, with a 2 × 2 large tile merged at the top left and at the bottom left, 10 tiles in all. The 2 large tiles and the 6 small tiles on the right hold 8 cameras; the remaining 2 small tiles hold a control panel and a clock.

Prerequisites: 8 cameras have been selected for the wall as described in “Choosing cameras and quality”, and the drag operation in “Drawing a custom layout” has been read. Time needed: about 3 minutes.

  1. In the LiveView Mix tab, tap Adjust the Layout, then tap Draw a custom layout.

    Check: The Custom layout page shows the starting shape: a 3 × 3 grid with a 2 × 2 large tile at the top left.

  2. Set Rows to 4 and Columns to 4.

    Check: The grid becomes 4 × 4, the large tile at the top left is kept, and Tiles shows 13.

  3. Drag one finger across the grid, over the 2 × 2 cells at the bottom left (the third and fourth rows, first and second columns).

    Check: The four cells are merged into a second large tile, and Tiles shows 10. The large tiles are numbered 1 and 6.

  4. Tap Use this layout, then tap Done.

    Check: The screen returns to the Adjust the Layout page, and the Custom diagram is selected.

  5. Tap Arrange the wall and drag the cameras to be enlarged onto the large tiles numbered 1 and 6.

    Check: The dragged camera and the content of the target tile swap places. For the arrangement, see “Arranging the wall and its slots”.

  6. On the Arrange page, add two empty slots and set one to Control and the other to Clock.

    Check: The canvas shows the control panel and the clock in the two slots. For the setup, see “What an empty slot can show”.

  7. Tap Done repeatedly to return to the LiveView Mix tab, turn the device sideways, and tap Full screen.

    Check: The wall shows two large tiles and eight small tiles of mixed sizes, as in the picture below.

Expected outcome: the wall follows the layout that was drawn, and the large tiles hold the important cameras. For control panels, see Chapter 9, “Control panels and webhooks”. The order of the slots, the positions of the large tiles and the content of the empty slots are stored on this device; when changing devices, a backup and restore can carry them along; see “LiveView Mix in Settings”.

Arranging the wall and its slots

Path: LiveView Mix › Adjust the Layout › Arrange the wall. This page decides what goes into each slot. Its title is Arrange. From top to bottom, the page holds the layout row, the canvas, Tips and the Order list. Arrange the wall is available as soon as cameras have been selected or a device exists.

  • Layout row: the same layout diagrams as on Adjust the Layout; the layout can be changed here directly. The Custom diagram appears once a layout has been drawn or while it is in use, and can only be selected here.
  • Canvas: always drawn in 16:9 landscape, showing the current page. The number of each slot is in its top-left corner. Camera slots show a live picture (SD); a camera that is offline or outside the plan shows a black tile with a crossed-out camera icon. While the watermark is off, the channel name is in the bottom-left corner; when it is on, the watermark is previewed. Control panels on the canvas look as they do on the wall; tapping one opens its editor and does not send a request. On a device held upright, the real wall is flipped, but the order is the same.
  • Unused tiles: shown with a dashed outline and a +. They are within one page of the selected layout and have no content yet.
  • Changing pages: when there are more slots than the layout holds, arrows and Page 1 of 2 appear below the canvas. Swiping left or right also changes the page.
  • Tips: a note that can be folded away. The folded state is remembered.
  • Order list: all slots in fill order, each with its number and its name and device; an empty slot shows the kind of content it holds.
  • Toolbar: Cancel in the top-left corner, Edit and Done in the top-right corner.

To swap the places of two slots:

  1. In the LiveView Mix tab, tap Adjust the Layout, then tap Arrange the wall.

    Check: The Arrange page opens.

  2. Drag a camera slot on the canvas with one finger onto another slot. Pressing and holding first is not needed.

    Check: The dragged slot lifts and follows the finger, and the target slot shows a highlighted frame.

  3. Lift the finger.

    Check: The two slots have swapped places, and the Order list is updated.

  • When a slot is dropped onto a dashed tile without content, the dragged slot moves to the end of the order.
  • When the finger leaves the canvas before it is lifted, the wall is unchanged.
  • To place a slot on another page, change to that page first and then drag; the slot numbers run on continuously across pages.
  • Tapping a camera slot does nothing; cameras are added and removed in Choose Cameras. Tapping an empty slot opens its editor; see “What an empty slot can show”.

To change the order, remove slots and add empty slots with the list:

  1. Tap Edit in the top-right corner.

    Check: Every row of the Order list shows a reorder handle and a remove button.

  2. Drag the reorder handle on the right of a row to a new position.

    Check: The order of the slots changes, and the numbers and the canvas are updated. The order can be changed across pages.

  3. To remove a slot, swipe a row to the left and tap Delete; in editing mode, the remove button of the row can be used as well.

    Check: The row disappears, and the slots behind it move forward. When a camera slot is removed, that camera is also unticked in Choose Cameras.

  4. Tap Add empty slot at the bottom of the list.

    Check: A new row Empty slot is added at the end of the list. When the current page is full, the new slot is on the next page, and the page must be changed before Tap to fill is visible.

  5. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The screen returns to the Adjust the Layout page, and the arrangement is kept.

  • An empty slot is always added at the end. To leave a gap in the middle, add an empty slot first and then drag it to the position wanted: the empty slot and the slot at that position swap places, and the camera that was there moves to the end.
  • Tapping Cancel in the top-left corner restores the wall to its state when the Arrange page was entered.

What an empty slot can show

An empty slot (Tap to fill) does not have to stay blank. Tap an empty slot on the canvas to open the Slot N page, and choose the content with the Shows menu:

ContentOptions and description
EmptyA plain colored space. Color selects the color; the default is black. Choosing Empty removes any picture, control panel, clock or label that the slot held.
ImageChoose Photo picks a picture from the photo library, and Take Photo takes one with the camera (not shown when the device has no camera). After a picture is chosen, Fill sets how it fills the slot: Default (the whole picture, possibly with black bars), Enlarge to fill (fills the slot, the edges are cropped) or Stretch to fill (fills the slot, the picture is distorted). Best size shows the size in pixels that the slot covers on a 3840 × 2160 screen. When a picture is already set, the button changes to Choose a Different Photo, and Remove Image appears. A picture is stored reduced to at most 512 pixels on its long side, so a picture in a large tile can look soft.
ControlA row of buttons; each button sends an HTTP request when it is tapped. For the setup of control panels and their buttons, see Chapter 9, “Control panels and webhooks”.
ClockShows the current time. Options: 24-hour (on by default; when off, the convention of the app language applies), Show seconds, Show date (on by default) and Show day of the week. The names of days and months follow the language of the app, and their order follows the convention of that language.
LabelText on several lines. Text holds the content, Icon names a system symbol that is shown above the text (SF Symbol (optional); empty means no symbol), and Text color and Background set the colors. The defaults are white text on a black background.
Changing the kind of content removes the previous content

When another kind is selected in the Shows menu, the previous content is removed at once. For example, changing Control to Clock removes the button settings of the control panel. Cancel in the top-left corner restores them.

To place a picture in an empty slot:

  1. On the Arrange page, tap an empty slot on the canvas that shows Tap to fill.

    Check: The Slot N page opens, with Shows set to Empty.

  2. Tap Shows and select Image.

    Check: The page shows the Image section with the Choose Photo button.

  3. Tap Choose Photo, then tap a photo in the photo selection screen of the system.

    Check: The page shows a preview of the picture, with Fill, Best size, Choose a Different Photo and Remove Image.

  4. In the Fill menu, select how the picture fills the slot.

    Check: The menu shows the chosen way.

  5. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The slot on the canvas shows the picture.

To place a clock in an empty slot:

  1. Tap an empty slot on the canvas and select Clock in the Shows menu.

    Check: The page shows the Clock section with 24-hour, Show seconds, Show date and Show day of the week.

  2. Switch each option on or off as needed.

    Check: The clock on the canvas reflects the settings at once.

  3. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes, and the canvas shows the clock.

To place a label in an empty slot:

  1. Tap an empty slot on the canvas and select Label in the Shows menu.

    Check: The page shows the Label section with Text, Icon, Text color and Background.

  2. Enter the text to be shown in the Text field.

    Check: The slot on the canvas shows the text.

  3. Optional: enter the name of a system symbol in the Icon field, and adjust the colors with Text color and Background.

    Check: The slot shows the symbol, and the colors change accordingly.

  4. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes, and the canvas shows the label.

Pictures, clocks and labels do not use the camera allowance of the plan; control panels do. See “How plan limits affect the wall”.

Watermark

Path: LiveView Mix › Adjust the Layout, then scroll to the Watermark section. The watermark overlays text on the picture of each camera slot, showing which camera of which device the picture comes from. On the full-screen wall, pictures carry no label by default, so the watermark is recommended when cameras of several devices share one wall.

OptionDescriptionDefault
Show watermarkThe main switch. The options below appear only when it is on.Off
PositionTop left, Top, Top right, Center, Bottom left, Bottom or Bottom right.Bottom right
Device nameShows the name of the device.On
Camera nameShows the name of the channel.On
IP addressShows the address of the camera itself; when the device does not report one, the address of the device.Off
OpacityA slider from 0.2 to 1.0.85
ColorThe color of the text.White
Text sizeA slider from 8 to 28.11
FontSystem, Rounded, Monospaced or Serif.System
LegibilityKeeps the text readable over the picture: Shadow, Outline, Backdrop (a semi-transparent plate behind the text) or None. When the background is too bright or too busy, use Backdrop.Shadow
PreviewPreviews the watermark on a light and a dark swatch. The sample names come from the first camera on the wall.—

  1. On the Adjust the Layout page, scroll down to the Watermark section and switch on Show watermark.

    Check: The section expands and shows the options.

  2. Select the Position, and switch on the names to be shown: Device name, Camera name or IP address.

    Check: The two swatches of Preview show the selected content and position.

  3. Adjust Opacity, Color, Text size, Font and Legibility.

    Check: Preview reflects the adjustments at once.

  4. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The page closes. The camera pictures in the preview, on the arrange canvas and on the full-screen wall show the watermark.

  • The watermark is drawn on camera slots only, not on control panels, pictures, clocks or labels.
  • When all three names are switched off, no text is shown.
  • The watermark does not intercept touches; tapping a picture behaves as before.
  • While the watermark is off, camera slots in the preview and on the arrange canvas show the channel number and name; the full-screen wall shows no label at all.

Black bars, edge-to-edge video and the angle of the device

Path: LiveView Mix › Adjust the Layout › Black bars on this wall. When the shape of a camera picture differs from the shape of its tile, black bars appear. Black bars on this wall decides how all camera pictures on the wall handle them. There are three options:

  • Default: the whole picture is shown, and black bars may appear.
  • Enlarge to fill: the picture is enlarged in proportion until it fills the tile. The edges are cropped, and there are no black bars.
  • Stretch to fill: the picture is stretched to fill the tile. Nothing is cropped and there are no black bars, but the picture is distorted.

  1. On the Adjust the Layout page, tap Black bars on this wall.

    Check: A menu lists Default, Enlarge to fill and Stretch to fill.

  2. Select an option.

    Check: The menu shows the selected option. The camera pictures in the preview and on the full-screen wall follow it.

  • This setting belongs to LiveView Mix only and is independent of the default under Settings › Picture › Black bars. Picture slots have their own Fill option.
  • The single-camera view that opens from the full-screen wall always shows the whole picture. The full-screen viewer of the preview has its own switch; see “Opening a single camera”.
  • Settings › Picture › Edge-to-Edge Video is on by default. It lets full-screen video extend under the Dynamic Island and the rounded corners of the screen for the largest picture. When it is off, the picture keeps clear of these areas, at the cost of black bars. The setting applies to the full-screen wall of LiveView Mix as well.

The angle of the device

The full-screen wall is not locked to an orientation. It rearranges itself with the angle of the device; no setting is needed.

Angle of the deviceWhat the wall looks like
Held sideways (wider than tall)The layout is shown as it is.
Held upright (taller than wide)The layout is flipped about its diagonal: 4 columns by 2 rows becomes 2 columns by 4 rows, and a large tile on the left moves to the top. The order of the slots does not change; it is still left to right, then top to bottom.
An area whose width equals its heightThe layout is not flipped.

The canvas on the Arrange page is always drawn in landscape; held upright, the real wall is flipped, but the order is the same.

The full-screen wall

Path: LiveView Mix › Full screen. The full-screen wall places all slots in the selected layout and fills the screen. The wall carries no labels unless the watermark is switched on.

  1. In the LiveView Mix tab, tap Full screen (the diagonal arrows icon) in the top-right corner.

    Check: The screen changes to the full-screen wall. The status bar is hidden, and a ✕ button (Close) is in the top-left corner.

  2. When the wall has several pages, swipe to the left.

    Check: The next page is shown, and the page dots at the bottom of the screen move to the next dot.

  3. Swipe to the right.

    Check: The previous page is shown again.

  4. Tap ✕ in the top-left corner.

    Check: The wall closes and the LiveView Mix tab is shown again.

  • Paging: when there are more slots than the layout holds, the wall is divided into pages. The number of pages is the number of slots divided by the tiles per page, rounded up. Positions that a page does not fill are black. With several pages, page dots appear at the bottom of the screen.
  • Opening page: the wall opens on the first page that has something to show. When a long wall begins with a run of slots that point at cameras that do not exist, it does not stop on a page that consists only of status texts.
  • Streams: only the page that is being looked at plays; neighboring pages are not connected, which saves bandwidth. Keep cameras connected between pages changes this; see “LiveView Mix in Settings”.
  • Tapping a camera: opens the single-camera view of that camera; see “Opening a single camera”.
  • Tapping a button of a control panel: sends the request. When the button is set to ask for confirmation first, a confirmation dialog appears; see Chapter 9, “Control panels and webhooks”.
  • Status texts: a slot that cannot be shown keeps its position and shows a status text; tapping it does nothing. See “When a slot cannot show a camera”.
  • The wall cannot be rearranged by dragging. To adjust the slots, return to Arrange; see “Arranging the wall and its slots”.
  • Screen: while live pictures are on the wall, the device does not lock the screen automatically.
  • Nothing to show: when there are no slots at all, the screen shows LiveView Mix is empty. When every slot points at a camera that is not on this device (for example after a restore from a backup before any device was added), the screen shows These cameras aren't on this device.

Opening a single camera

Tapping a camera on the wall or in the preview opens a large picture of that camera. The two entry points open different screens.

From the full-screen wall

The screen is the single-camera view of that camera, always playing in HD. In the top-left corner are the back button ‹ (Back) and the camera name. When the device supports recording playback, the Recordings button is in the top-right corner. When the camera supports PTZ, a PTZ pad is in the bottom-right corner. When the picture carries sound, a speaker button (Mute, Unmute) is in the bottom-left corner. This view has no SD and HD switch and no black-bar switch.

  1. On the full-screen wall, tap the picture of a camera.

    Check: The screen changes to the single-camera view of that camera.

  2. Spread two fingers apart on the picture.

    Check: The picture is enlarged, up to 5 times. While it is enlarged, dragging with one finger moves the picture.

  3. Double-tap the picture.

    Check: The picture is enlarged to 2 times; another double-tap returns it to its original size.

  4. When the device supports recording playback, tap Recordings in the top-right corner.

    Check: The screen opens the picture and the recording playback of that camera, with Done in the top-right corner. For the operation, see Chapter 6, “Single-camera view” and Chapter 7, “Recording playback and speed”.

  5. Tap the back button ‹ in the top-left corner.

    Check: The screen shows the full-screen wall again. A camera head that is still turning stops. For PTZ control, see “PTZ control: moving the camera”.

From the preview

The screen is the full-screen viewer: one camera at a time, and swiping left or right changes to the next camera. The cameras that can be reached are those in the preview that can play (online, within the plan and not paused), in the same order as on the wall. Page dots are at the bottom of the screen.

  • ✕ (Close): closes the viewer and returns to the preview.
  • The camera name is at the top center.
  • The HD / SD button in the top-right corner switches the quality; the text on the button is the current quality. The viewer always opens in HD, and a switch applies to the current viewing only and is not saved.
  • The black-bar button in the top-right corner switches between Default and Stretch to fill, again for the current viewing only. When the black-bar setting of the wall is anything other than Default, the viewer starts on Stretch to fill.
  • The speaker button in the bottom-left corner appears only when the picture carries sound.

Tapping a camera in the preview that the plan does not cover (Not in your plan) opens the plans page; see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”. Tapping a camera that is offline, disabled or paused does nothing. Sound plays only in the single-camera view and in this full-screen viewer; for switching it on, see Chapter 6, “Single-camera view”.

When a slot cannot show a camera

A camera that cannot be shown keeps its position on the wall, and its slot shows a dark plate with a status text. Because the position is kept, the slots behind it do not move.

DisplayMeaningWhat to do
No signalThe device reports the channel as offline.Check the power and the network of the camera; see Chapter 15, “Troubleshooting”.
DisabledThe channel has not been enabled.Enable the channel on the device page or in Settings › Choose which cameras show; see Chapter 4, “The Devices tab and channels”.
Not in your planThe channel is enabled but exceeds the allowance of the current plan.See “How plan limits affect the wall” and Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.
PausedThe channel was paused with Pause Video; the slot shows a gray plate.Resume it with Resume Video on the device page; see Chapter 4, “The Devices tab and channels”.
Camera removedThe slot points at a camera that Cam Hub no longer has.Handle it with Empty Those Slots on the Choose Cameras page; see “Choosing cameras and quality”.
  • While a tile is connecting, it shows a spinning circle. When the connection fails, the tile explains the reason in a short text; a temporary failure is retried automatically.
  • While Keep cameras connected between pages is off, a tile first shows only the camera name at the moment its page comes into view, and the picture follows.
  • Hide offline cameras in Settings applies to the walls of the Live tab only. It does not remove slots from LiveView Mix.
  • Deleting a device in the app removes the slots that belong to it from the wall. The slots behind them move forward, and so do control panels.

How plan limits affect the wall

LiveView Mix itself does not limit the number of cameras on the wall. The number of channels that can show a picture at the same time is decided by the plan; for the details of the allowances, see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.

  • Free plan: at most 2 enabled channels across the whole app (single cameras and recorder channels together), and at most 1 recorder. A channel beyond the allowance shows Disabled on the wall; a channel that is enabled but exceeds the allowance shows Not in your plan. In both cases, the position of the slot is kept.
  • Camera plans and recorder plans: these raise the number of single cameras that can be enabled and the number of recorders, respectively. With a recorder plan, all channels of the subscribed recorders can be used.
  • Enabling channels: after a plan is upgraded, channels that were disabled are not enabled automatically; they must be switched on on the device page or in Settings › Choose which cameras show. A plan with no limit on either axis enables all channels automatically, and Choose which cameras show is then not shown in Settings.
  • Control panels use the allowance: each control panel on the wall counts as one single camera against the camera allowance of the plan, and not against the recorder allowance. When the allowance is not enough, the control panel stays in place, but its buttons are locked and the slot shows Not in your plan. On the Free plan, a control panel can therefore cost one camera its picture. Pictures, clocks and labels do not use the allowance.
  • Locked channels: tapping a camera in the preview that the plan does not cover opens the plans page. On the Choose Cameras page and on the arrange canvas, these channels show no live picture.
  • Custom layouts: at most 8 × 8, which is 64 tiles; see “Drawing a custom layout”.

LiveView Mix in Settings

Path: Settings › LiveView Mix. At the end of the row in the LiveView Mix section, the number of selected cameras is shown (6 cameras); before setup, the row shows Not set up. Tapping the row opens a page that holds the camera selection, the full-screen layout, the watermark and paging on one page. The options work as described in the sections above. Cancel in the top-left corner restores everything changed since the page was entered, and Done in the top-right corner keeps the changes.

Open on launch

Open on launch decides which screen the app shows when it starts:

  • Last viewed (the default).
  • LiveView Mix: opens the LiveView Mix tab.
  • LiveView Mix Full Screen: opens the LiveView Mix tab and goes straight into the full-screen wall after the start, once. Tapping ✕ returns to the preview in the tab.
  • Each device: opens the Live tab and shows that device.

The options LiveView Mix and LiveView Mix Full Screen appear only after the wall has been set up.

  1. Tap the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen and scroll to the LiveView Mix section.

    Check: The screen shows the LiveView Mix row and the Open on launch menu.

  2. Tap Open on launch.

    Check: The screen shows the list of options, with the current option ticked.

  3. Select LiveView Mix Full Screen.

    Check: The menu shows LiveView Mix Full Screen. The next time the app starts, it goes straight into the full-screen wall.

Keep cameras connected between pages

Keep cameras connected between pages in the Paging section is off by default. When it is on, pages that are not being looked at stay connected, so the picture appears at once when swiping instead of a black tile while the camera reconnects. The cost is more bandwidth and battery; the effect is largest for recorders that sign in with a session. At most 12 streams are kept. When the switch is turned off, the kept connections are closed at once. The switch applies to the streams of the whole app.

  1. On the Adjust the Layout page, scroll down to the Paging section.

    Check: The screen shows the Keep cameras connected between pages switch with its explanation.

  2. Switch on Keep cameras connected between pages.

    Check: The switch is on.

Backup and restore

The settings of the wall (the selected cameras and their order, the layout, the custom layout, the watermark, the content of empty slots and pictures) belong to the app settings and are stored with an iCloud backup; when cameras are exported, switching on Include app settings carries them along as well. On restore, slots that belong to a device that does not exist on the new device are not kept. For the procedure, see Chapter 10, “Sharing and backup”.

Differences on Apple TV

Apple TV shows a wall that was built on an iPhone or an iPad. Arranging the wall, editing its slots and drawing a custom layout are done on the iPhone or iPad; see Chapter 14, “Apple TV”.

9Control panels and webhooks

A control panel is a tile on a LiveView Mix wall that holds a row of buttons. Each button sends an HTTP request to an address of choice when pressed, which suits a Home Assistant webhook or service call, a relay board, Node-RED, or any other HTTP service the phone can reach.

What a control panel does

A control panel consists of a title, a number of buttons and an optional clock. Each button stores one complete HTTP request: method, URL, headers and body. When a button is pressed, the request goes directly from this iPhone, iPad or Apple TV to the address, without passing through a Cam Hub server.

  • Cam Hub only sends the request. The URL and the content are entirely the choice of the user. Cam Hub does not check what kind of service answers, and it is not a dedicated controller for any smart-home product.
  • A request is sent only when a button is pressed on the wall. Tapping a panel on the arrange screen opens its editor and sends nothing.
  • Control panels are created and edited on iPhone and iPad. Apple TV displays and runs the panels that exist; see “How a panel looks on the wall”.
A control panel uses one camera allowance

Like a standalone camera, each control panel uses one camera allowance of the plan. When the allowance is not sufficient, the panel is locked and its buttons are unavailable. For details, see “What uses allowance”.

Adding a control panel to the wall

Prerequisite: LiveView Mix has been set up and the wall holds at least one camera; for the setup, see “Building a first wall of six cameras”. While it has not been set up, Arrange the wall can also be reached through Settings › LiveView Mix as soon as a device has been added.

  1. Tap the LiveView Mix tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the preview wall, with three buttons in the top-right corner.

  2. Tap the Adjust the Layout button, the rightmost of the three buttons in the top-right corner.

    Check: The Adjust the Layout page opens.

  3. Tap Arrange the wall.

    Check: The Arrange page opens: the canvas of the wall is at the top, and the Order list below it lists every tile in sequence.

  4. Scroll to the bottom of the list and tap Add empty slot.

    Check: The list gains a row Empty slot, and the canvas gains a tile marked Tap to fill. The new tile is added at the end. When the current page is full, the tile is on the next page; use the arrows below the canvas or swipe sideways to change pages.

  5. Tap the tile marked Tap to fill on the canvas.

    Check: The editor of the tile opens from the bottom of the screen, with a title such as Slot 9. The first row is Shows, and its current value is Empty.

  6. Tap Shows and select Control in the menu.

    Check: The page shows the three sections Template, Panel and Buttons. The template is Gate / Shutter, the panel title is Gate, and the button section holds three buttons, each with No endpoint set in orange below it.

  7. Tap Template and select the closest type.

    Check: The button section is replaced by the default buttons of that template. For the content of the templates, see “Templates”.

  8. In the Panel section, enter the name of the panel in the Title field.

    Check: The field shows the name, which is later displayed above the buttons of the panel.

  9. Optional: tap Color and select the color of the border and the buttons.

    Check: The color icon shows the selected color. The default is cyan.

  10. Optional: turn on Show the time.

    Check: Four switches appear: Seconds, Date, Day of the week and 24-hour. The clock is shown in the space below the buttons.

  11. Set the URL and the content of every button as described in “Setting up a button”.

    Check: Every row of the button section shows the host name of the URL below its label, instead of No endpoint set.

  12. Tap Done in the top-right corner of the tile editor.

    Check: The screen returns to the Arrange page, and the tile on the canvas shows the panel as it appears on the wall.

  13. Tap Done in the top-right corner of the Arrange page.

    Check: The screen returns to the Adjust the Layout page.

  14. Tap Done in the top-right corner of the Adjust the Layout page.

    Check: The screen returns to the LiveView Mix tab, and the preview wall shows the new control panel.

  • When an empty tile already exists, skip step 4 and tap the empty tile on the canvas.
  • Tapping Cancel in the top-left corner of the tile editor restores the whole wall to the state it had when the editor was opened, including every change to the buttons.
  • Changing Shows to another item clears the title and all buttons of the panel. To remove the panel and keep the tile, set Shows to Empty. To remove the whole tile, swipe the row to the left in the list on the Arrange page.
  • For picture, clock and label tiles, see “What an empty slot can show”.
  • When Arrange the wall is reached through Settings › LiveView Mix, the operation that follows is the same.

Templates

The Template menu offers eleven templates. A template only determines the default title, the number of buttons, their icons and the initial setting of Confirm before firing. No template contains a URL; every button needs its own URL.
