The title is replaced only when it is still empty or still the default title of the previous template; a title typed by the user stays unchanged. Select the template first, then adjust the details.
  • The initial template of a newly added control panel is Gate / Shutter.

The settings of a panel

ItemDescription
ShowsThe content of the tile: Empty, Image, Control, Clock or Label. Selecting Control turns the tile into a control panel.
TemplateSee “Templates”.
TitleShown above the buttons, to say what the panel controls. When empty, no title is shown.
ColorThe color of the border and of the buttons of the panel.
Show the timeShows the current time in the space below the buttons. When on, Seconds, Date, Day of the week and 24-hour can be selected. Names of days and months follow the language of the app.
ButtonsThe list of buttons. Tap a row to edit that button, swipe a row to the left to delete it, and tap Add Button to add a blank button at the end. The list cannot be reordered; to change the sequence, delete a button and add it again. Each row shows the icon, the label and the host name of the URL; while no valid URL is entered, No endpoint set is shown in orange instead. When the label is empty, the row shows Button.

Setting up a button

Prerequisite: the editor of the tile is open as described in “Adding a control panel to the wall”, and Control is selected.

  1. In the Buttons section, tap the button to set up. To create a new button, tap Add Button first, then tap the new row.

    Check: The screen shows the editor of that button. Its title is the label of the button, and the top-left corner holds only a back arrow.

  2. In the row of icons below the Icon row, tap the icon to use, or type the name of an SF Symbols icon in the field on the right.

    Check: The Icon row shows the selected icon and its name, for example arrow.up.to.line.

  3. Enter the text to show below the icon in the Label field.

    Check: The field shows the text. The title of the page changes to the same text.

  4. For a button that must be confirmed before it runs, turn on Confirm before firing.

    Check: The switch is on. A confirmation box now appears when the button is pressed; see “Pressing a button and reading the result”.

  5. In the Request section, select GET, POST, PUT or DELETE in the Method menu.

    Check: The menu shows the selected method. With GET, the Body section is absent from the lower part of the page; the other three methods show it.

  6. Enter the complete URL in the field below Method, beginning with http:// or https://.

    Check: The field shows the URL.

  7. When a header is needed, tap Add Header and enter the name and the value of the header in the Name and Value fields.

    Check: The Headers section gains a row, and both fields show the text entered. Repeat the step for further headers; swipe a row to the left to delete the header.

  8. When content must be sent, confirm the content type in the upper field of the Body section (application/json by default), then enter the content in the text box below it.

    Check: The text box shows the content. The content is sent exactly as typed.

  9. Tap the back arrow in the top-left corner.

    Check: The screen returns to the tile editor, and the row of the button shows the host name of the URL below its label.

FieldDescription
IconTwenty common icons below the row can be tapped directly. The name of any SF Symbols icon can be typed as well.
LabelShown below the icon, and used as the text of the red button in the confirmation box. When the label is empty, the button shows only the icon, and the red button of the confirmation box reads Confirm.
Confirm before firingWhen on, pressing the button first opens a confirmation box. Buttons that make physical equipment move, such as opening a door, unlocking and alarms, should have it on.
MethodGET, POST, PUT or DELETE; the default is POST. GET sends no body.
URLMust begin with http:// or https:// and contain a host name or address. Spaces at the beginning and the end are ignored. Query parameters are written in the URL itself. When the URL is empty or malformed, pressing the button shows a failure.
HeadersAny number of names and values. Rows with an empty name are skipped. A Content-Type header entered here takes precedence over the content type field of the Body section.
BodyShown only for POST, PUT and DELETE. The upper field is the content type, application/json by default; the text box below it is the content. An empty content sends no body. The value of the content type field is attached only when the content is not empty and no Content-Type header has been entered.

Pressing a button and reading the result

Buttons can be pressed on the preview wall of the LiveView Mix tab and on the full-screen wall. A newly configured button has no separate test function; pressing it once serves as the test, followed by a check on the receiving side that the request arrived.

  1. On the preview wall or the full-screen wall, tap a button of the panel.

    Check: A button without Confirm before firing changes its icon to a spinner immediately, which means that the request has been sent. A button with it on opens a confirmation box beside the panel.

  2. When the confirmation box appears, tap the red button in it, which carries the label of the pressed button. To cancel, tap anywhere outside the box.

    Check: The box closes and the icon changes to a spinner. When canceled, no request is sent.

  3. Watch the icon of the button.

    Check: Depending on the result, the icon changes to a green check mark or an orange warning triangle, and returns to the original icon after about 1.6 seconds.

The button showsMeaning
The configured iconIdle, or the result has been displayed.
A spinnerThe request has been sent and the answer is awaited. When no answer arrives within 10 seconds, the request counts as failed.
A green check markThe receiving side answered with a status code from 200 to 299. Redirects are followed automatically, and the final answer decides.
An orange warning triangleThe request did not succeed. The cause can be an empty or malformed URL, no connection, a timeout, an untrusted certificate, or a status code outside 200 to 299, for example 401, 404 or 500. The screen does not show the cause, and no log is kept.
  • A green check mark only means that the receiving side answered successfully. It does not prove that the equipment moved. To verify the outcome, look at the log of the receiving side.
  • Every press sends one request, and nothing prevents repeated presses. Pressing twice in a row sends two requests. Buttons that make physical equipment move should have Confirm before firing on.
  • When the orange triangle appears repeatedly, check in this order: whether the URL is valid, whether the phone and the receiving side are on the same network or can reach each other, and whether the address of the receiving side can be resolved. When the receiving side is on the local network, Cam Hub must be allowed to access the local network; see “Finding devices with the network scan”. For other problems, see Chapter 15, “Troubleshooting”.

How a panel looks on the wall

  • Button layout: 1 button is placed in 1 column, 2 buttons in 2 columns, 3 buttons in 3 columns, 4 buttons as 2 × 2, and 5 or more buttons in 3 columns.
  • Small tiles: the panel shrinks automatically. The clock is hidden first, then the labels below the icons; the title and the icons remain.
  • Plan: each control panel uses one camera allowance. A panel beyond the allowance shows a lock, its title and Not in your plan, and its buttons are unavailable. Clock, label, picture and empty tiles use no allowance. A subscription to an NVR plan alone does not raise the allowance available to panels. For the counting rules, see “What uses allowance”.
  • Apple TV: a panel is created on an iPhone or an iPad, and it is shown on the wall of the Apple TV; see Chapter 14, “Apple TV”.
  • Backup and sharing: the settings of a panel, including the values of headers, belong to the app settings. They enter every iCloud backup, and they also enter a sharing code when Include app settings is on during export; see Chapter 10, “Sharing and backup”.

Using Home Assistant

The following two approaches use Home Assistant as the example. The address homeassistant.local, the identifier gate-open-7f3c9a21 and the entity name cover.gate are sample values and must be replaced with the real ones. The behavior on the Home Assistant side is defined by its own documentation and can change between versions.

Prerequisites: Home Assistant runs on the home network and the phone can reach its address; a tile of the LiveView Mix wall has Control selected (see “Adding a control panel to the wall”). Home Assistant uses http and port 8123 by default. The sample text in the URL field of the app begins with https and must be changed to match the real setup.

Approach 1: webhook trigger (no token needed)

  1. In Home Assistant, create a new automation.

    Check: The screen shows the editor of the automation.

  2. Select Webhook as the trigger and enter an identifier that is hard to guess, for example gate-open-7f3c9a21.

    Check: The editor shows the identifier. The identifier works like a password: anyone who knows it and the address can start the automation.

  3. Set the action, for example the entity that opens the gate, and save the automation.

    Check: The automation appears in the list of automations of Home Assistant.

  4. In Cam Hub, open the editor of the button to use, as described in step 1 of “Setting up a button”.

    Check: The screen shows the editor of that button.

  5. Select POST as the Method and enter http://homeassistant.local:8123/api/webhook/gate-open-7f3c9a21 in the URL field. Headers and body can stay empty.

    Check: The field shows the URL, and after returning, the row of the button shows the host name homeassistant.local.

  6. Return to the wall and press the button.

    Check: The icon shows a spinner first, then a green check mark.

  7. In Home Assistant, open the run log of the automation.

    Check: The log shows the run that the press started. Home Assistant can also answer successfully for an identifier that does not exist, so the run log decides, not the green check mark.

The equivalent request is:

POST /api/webhook/gate-open-7f3c9a21 HTTP/1.1
Host: homeassistant.local:8123

The automation can also be written as a configuration file. The following example is for comparison only, and the syntax depends on the version of Home Assistant:

triggers:
  - trigger: webhook
    webhook_id: gate-open-7f3c9a21
    allowed_methods:
      - POST
    local_only: true
actions:
  - action: cover.open_cover
    target:
      entity_id: cover.gate

A webhook trigger accepts only POST and PUT by default, and by default only requests from the local network. Using it from an outside network needs separate measures; see “Security notes”.

Approach 2: service call (token needed)

  1. On the profile page of Home Assistant, create a long-lived access token and copy it immediately.

    Check: The screen shows the token. A token is usually displayed in full only once, when it is created.

  2. In Cam Hub, open the editor of the button, select POST as the Method and enter http://homeassistant.local:8123/api/services/cover/open_cover in the URL field.

    Check: The field shows the URL.

  3. Tap Add Header.

    Check: The Headers section gains a row with the two fields Name and Value.

  4. Enter Authorization in the Name field, and Bearer, a space and the copied token in the Value field.

    Check: Both fields show the text entered. The value of the header is displayed in plain text.

  5. In the Body section, confirm that the content type is application/json and enter {"entity_id":"cover.gate"} in the text box.

    Check: The text box shows the content.

  6. Return to the wall and press the button.

    Check: The icon shows a spinner first, then a green check mark. The log of Home Assistant shows that the service was called.

The equivalent request is:

POST /api/services/cover/open_cover HTTP/1.1
Host: homeassistant.local:8123
Authorization: Bearer <long-lived access token>
Content-Type: application/json

{"entity_id":"cover.gate"}
Prefer the webhook trigger

When a webhook identifier leaks, the effect is limited to the one automation it belongs to. A long-lived access token can operate the whole of Home Assistant. For any action that approach 1 can perform, use approach 1.

Security notes

TopicDescription and recommendation
HTTP and HTTPSA request sent with http:// is not encrypted. Anyone on the same network path can read the URL, the token in a header and the body. Use HTTP only inside a trusted home network and for webhooks that carry no sensitive data. Whenever a request carries a token or leaves the home network, use https://.
HTTPS certificatesCam Hub has no option to trust a self-signed certificate. An https:// address with a self-signed certificate fails, and the button shows the orange triangle. Inside the local network, http:// can be used instead, or a certificate that the phone trusts can be installed on the receiving side.
Storage of tokens and identifiersThe values of headers are displayed in plain text in the editor and are stored in plain text in the app settings of this device.
Backups and sharing codesThe settings of a panel enter every iCloud backup, and every sharing code exported with Include app settings on. Treat such a code like a password and lock it with a PIN or a password; see “Locking a code”. When a token has been exposed, revoke it on the receiving side and create a new one.
Outside networksOpening port 8123 of Home Assistant directly to the internet is not recommended. When away from home, use a VPN or the official remote-access method of Home Assistant, and change the URL to the matching address.
Physical actionsTurn on Confirm before firing for buttons that open doors, unlock and sound alarms. Cam Hub has no further lock on panel buttons; anyone who can operate the unlocked device can press them.
Name resolutionNames ending in .local may not resolve on some networks. When connections fail, enter the fixed IP address of the receiving side instead.

10Sharing and backup

Devices with their passwords, and optionally the app settings (LiveView Mix walls and control panels), can be moved to another device or shared with other people as an encrypted code, or backed up to iCloud and restored on one's own iPhone, iPad and Apple TV.

Comparing the two methods

TopicSharing codeiCloud backup
WhereSettings › Export Cameras and Settings › Import Cameras, in the Share Cameras sectionSettings › Back Up to iCloud and Settings › Restore from iCloud, in the Backup & Restore section
iCloud neededNo. The code travels by any means the user chooses.Yes. Both devices must be signed in to iCloud with the same Apple Account.
Choice of devicesThe devices to export can be ticked.All devices.
App settingsOptional; included only when Include app settings is on.Always included.
LockNo lock, a six-digit PIN, or a password.No PIN. Encrypted with a key built into the app.
Devices that can use itCam Hub of other people, and one's own iPhone and iPad. Apple TV can only import.One's own iPhone, iPad and Apple TV.
Typical useSharing with other people, or two devices that do not share an Apple Account.Changing phones, or bringing the settings to Apple TV.

Exporting cameras (creating a code)

Prerequisite: at least one device has been added. While there is no device, Export Cameras is unavailable.

  1. Tap the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the settings list.

  2. In the Share Cameras section, tap Export Cameras.

    Check: The Export Cameras page opens: the Devices to export list (all ticked by default), Lock with a PIN, Include app settings, and a button such as Export 5 devices.

  3. Optional: tap a device row to clear or restore its tick. The Deselect all button at the right of the list title clears every tick.

    Check: The button shows the number of selected devices, for example Export 3 devices. While no device is selected, the button is unavailable and the button at the right of the list title reads Select all.

  4. Optional: turn on Include app settings.

    Check: The switch is on, and the explanation below it changes to say that the code also carries the app settings, the same as restoring from iCloud. For the items carried, see “What backups and codes contain”.

  5. Optional: set the lock as described in “Locking a code”.

    Check: After a lock has been set, Export 3 devices stays unavailable until the entry is complete. Without a lock, the code is open: anyone who has the code and Cam Hub can import it.

  6. Tap the export button, for example Export 3 devices.

    Check: The result page opens with the title Export Cameras. Its top part explains that the code contains the cameras and their passwords, encrypted; below it are the buttons Share and Copy, and below those the full text of the code.

  7. Tap Share and select a way to send, or tap Copy.

    Check: Tapping Share opens the system share sheet, with options such as Messages, Mail or AirDrop. Tapping Copy changes the button to Copied, and the complete text of the code is on the clipboard.

  8. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The result page closes and the Export Cameras page is shown again.

  • Share sends a link, Copy copies text. Share sends a link that begins with https://cam-hub.almx.cc/i#, with the code after the “#”, which browsers do not send to the web server. Copy places the complete text on the clipboard.
  • The recipient: when Cam Hub is installed, opening the link opens the import page directly with the code filled in. When it is not installed, the link opens a web page that points to the download page of the app and shows the code for copying.
  • The text of the code begins with a short English explanation and the install address, followed by the code, which begins with CAMHUB1:, CAMHUB1L: or CAMHUB2: and can be thousands of characters long. When importing, the whole text can be pasted, or the code alone.
  • A code contains the passwords of the devices. A code does not expire, and deleting the devices or the app on the source device does not invalidate a code that has already been shared. When a code may have been exposed, change the passwords of the devices concerned.
A code hands over the passwords of the devices

Anyone who obtains a code without a lock and has Cam Hub can import every device in it with its password. Send the code only to people who are trusted, and set a lock when needed.

Locking a code

A code can be open, locked with a six-digit PIN, or locked with a password (Complex encryption). The strength of the protection differs greatly between the three, and the choice depends on how the code is sent.

TopicOpenSix-digit PINPassword (complex encryption)
How to setBoth switches stay off (default)Turn on Lock with a PINTurn on Lock with a PIN, then turn on Complex encryption
What to enterNothingSix digits, on the numeric keypad8 characters or more, any characters, on the full keyboard, entered twice
The code begins withCAMHUB1:CAMHUB1L:CAMHUB2:
When importingImports directlyThe Enter PIN dialog appearsThe Enter password dialog appears
StrengthThe encryption key is built into the app, so any Cam Hub of the same version can open the code. It only keeps the contents from being read at a glance. It does not protect against anyone who has both the code and the app.Encrypted with the PIN, using PBKDF2 (600,000 rounds) and AES-256-GCM. A PIN has only a million possibilities, so someone who obtains the code can try them all offline on their own computer. It protects against casual access, not against a determined person.The same encryption, with the key derived from the password. Only a long password that is not used elsewhere makes guessing impractical.
Older appsImports with an app of the same versionImports with an app of the same versionAn older app that does not know the format shows Update Cam Hub and must be updated first

Locking with a six-digit PIN

  1. On the Export Cameras page, turn on Lock with a PIN.

    Check: The field PIN (6 digits) appears below the switch, and the explanation changes to say that whoever imports must enter this PIN and that it must be sent separately from the code.

  2. Enter six digits.

    Check: The field accepts digits only, the keypad closes after the sixth digit, and the export button becomes available. With fewer digits, the export button stays unavailable.

Locking with a password (complex encryption)

  1. On the Export Cameras page, turn on Lock with a PIN.

    Check: The Complex encryption switch and the PIN (6 digits) field appear.

  2. Turn on Complex encryption.

    Check: The PIN field is replaced by the two fields Password (8+ characters) and Confirm password, and anything typed earlier is cleared.

  3. Enter the password in the Password (8+ characters) field.

    Check: The field masks the characters with dots. Any letters, numbers and symbols can be used, and a longer password is stronger.

  4. Enter the same password again in the Confirm password field.

    Check: When both entries match and have at least 8 characters, the export button becomes available. When they differ, the orange text The two passwords don't match. appears below the field and the button stays unavailable.

  • Send the PIN or the password separately from the code, never in the same message.
  • A forgotten PIN or password cannot be recovered. Cam Hub does not store it and does not send it to the developer. When it is forgotten, export a new code.
  • A password is case-sensitive, and spaces count. The same accented letter typed on different keyboards is treated as identical.
  • When a code is placed somewhere that is not private, such as a chat group or an e-mail, lock it with a password and send the password by another channel.
  • The person who imports does not need to know in advance which lock was used. After the code is pasted, Cam Hub recognizes the lock itself and shows the matching prompt and keyboard; see “Importing cameras”.

Importing cameras

Where: Settings › Import Cameras, or directly by tapping a received sharing link.

Pasting a code

  1. Tap the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the settings list.

  2. In the Share Cameras section, tap Import Cameras.

    Check: The Import Cameras page opens. The section title is Paste the code, with the buttons Paste and Import Cameras and a text box.

  3. Tap Paste. Alternatively, touch and hold in the text box and paste manually.

    Check: The code appears in the text box. When the code is locked, a lock note appears below the buttons: Locked with a 6-digit PIN — you'll be asked for it. or Locked with a password — you'll be asked for it. An open code shows no note.

  4. Tap Import Cameras.

    Check: An open code is imported directly, and the screen shows Added 3 cameras. A locked code opens the Enter PIN dialog (numeric keypad, field 6 digits) or the Enter password dialog (full keyboard).

  5. For a locked code, enter the PIN or the password and tap Import.

    Check: The dialog closes and the screen shows Added 3 cameras.

  6. Tap Done.

    Check: The screen returns to the settings list, and the added devices appear in the Devices tab.

When Paste is tapped, the system can ask whether Cam Hub may paste from another app; allow it. Alternatively, touch and hold in the text box and paste with the edit menu.

Importing from a link

  1. On an iPhone or iPad that has Cam Hub, tap the received sharing link.

    Check: Cam Hub opens the Import Cameras page with the code already in the text box. For a locked code, the matching lock note is shown.

  2. Tap Import Cameras and, for a locked code, enter the PIN or the password.

    Check: The screen shows Added 3 cameras.

Message when importingMeaning and action
Added 3 camerasThe import is complete. The number is the number of imported devices; a recorder counts as one.
Wrong PINThe PIN is not correct. Ask the sender for the six digits, then tap Import Cameras again and re-enter it.
Wrong passwordThe password is not correct. Capitals, spaces and symbols must match exactly.
Update Cam HubThe code was made with a different version of Cam Hub, or it uses a format that this version does not know. Update the app on both devices and try again.
Couldn't read that codeThe pasted content is not a code, the code is incomplete, or it has been damaged. Make sure the whole code has been pasted.
The cameras could not be saved. Try again.The code itself was readable, but writing the devices failed. Try again.
  • Importing merges. A device that matches a device already on this device has its name, address, account, password and channels replaced by the contents of the code; the other devices are added. Other devices already on this device are not deleted.
  • The enabled state of channels is limited again by the plan of this device. Channels beyond the allowance are imported as Disabled. For the allowances, see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.
  • App settings: settings are applied only for a code that was exported with Include app settings on. They then replace the matching settings on this device, including the LiveView Mix wall and the language. Tiles of the wall that point to devices not imported with the code are removed, and the following tiles move up. A code without app settings leaves the settings of this device unchanged.

What backups and codes contain

ItemiCloud backupSharing code
DevicesAll devicesThe ticked devices
Data of each deviceName, address, ports, username, password, connection method, model, serial number, firmware version, and the position of the device in the list.
ChannelsChannel names and custom names, the enabled state, the paused state.
App settingsAlways includedIncluded only when Include app settings is on

The app settings comprise: the language; the LiveView Mix wall, including the layout, tile pictures and control panels (with the values of their headers); the choice in Open on launch; Default quality, Black bars, Edge-to-Edge Video and Hide offline cameras; the sound preference; the range of the network scan; the option of LiveView Mix to keep cameras connected between pages; and the saved sign-in of cloud-connected cameras.

Not included: the plan and subscription state (it follows the Apple Account and is retrieved with Restore Purchases; see “Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code”), saved device reports, and anything not listed above.

Backing up to iCloud

Prerequisite: this device is signed in to iCloud in the system settings. Without a sign-in, the backup stays on this device and does not reach other devices.

  1. Tap the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the settings list.

  2. In the Backup & Restore section, tap Back Up to iCloud.

    Check: The iCloud Backup page opens: the Destination selector at the top, then the Current Backup section and the Back Up Now button. While no backup exists, the section shows No backup in iCloud yet.

  3. In Destination, select My Backup or Apple TV.

    Check: The explanation below the selector changes. My Backup is explained as one's own backup for moving to a new iPhone or iPad; Apple TV is explained as a separate copy that an Apple TV restores. Current Backup now shows the information of the selected destination.

  4. Tap Back Up Now.

    Check: A spinner appears beside the button. When the backup is complete, the page shows the green text Backed up 3 recorders · 2 cameras to iCloud., and Current Backup shows the new Last backed up time and the number of devices.

  • The two destinations are independent. My Backup and Apple TV are two separate copies, and backing up to one does not change the other. Each destination keeps only the latest copy; a new backup replaces the old one.
  • An iPhone and an iPad can restore either copy; an Apple TV can restore only the Apple TV copy. After devices or the wall have been changed on an iPhone or iPad, back up to Apple TV again so that the television receives the new content.
  • The size of a backup is limited to about 1 MB. A wall with many tile pictures can exceed the limit. The page then shows Backup failed. Check iCloud is signed in and try again., and some tile pictures must be removed before backing up again.
  • After a successful backup, the system can show a request for a rating, which can be dismissed.
  • Back up before deleting all data. Delete All Data removes every device and saved password from this device. An iCloud backup is not affected and can be restored afterwards as described in “Restoring from iCloud”. Without an iCloud backup, the device passwords cannot be recovered. See Chapter 13, “Settings”.
How a backup is encrypted and protected

A backup is stored encrypted in the private iCloud of the user and is synced only to devices that use the same Apple Account. A backup has no PIN. The encryption key is built into the app and is the same in every installation, so every one of one's own devices can restore without a password to remember. The key only prevents the backup from being stored as plain text; it is not a secret kept from someone who obtains both the backup and the app. The protection of a backup rests on the security of the Apple Account and of iCloud, so the Apple Account must be kept secure.

Restoring from iCloud

Prerequisite: this device is signed in with the Apple Account to which the backup belongs, and a backup exists in iCloud. Right after a backup, it can take some time before it syncs to another device.

  1. Tap the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the settings list.

  2. In the Backup & Restore section, tap Restore from iCloud.

    Check: The Restore from iCloud page opens with the Source selector, the iCloud Backup section and the Restore button. When no backup is found, the section shows No backup found in iCloud. Back up from your iPhone first, signed in to the same Apple Account. and the Restore button is unavailable.

  3. In Source, select My Backup or Apple TV.

    Check: The iCloud Backup section shows the time of creation (From) and the number of Devices of that backup.

  4. Tap Restore.

    Check: A spinner appears beside the button. When the restore is complete, the page shows the green text Restored 5 devices.

  • Devices are merged: a device that matches a device already on this device is updated, including the names and the enabled state of its channels; the other devices are added. Other devices already present are not deleted.
  • App settings: the settings in the backup replace the matching settings on this device, including the LiveView Mix wall, Open on launch and the language. Settings that are not in the backup stay unchanged. Tiles of the wall that point to devices that were not restored are removed, and the following tiles move up; empty tiles, control panels, clocks, labels and picture tiles are kept.
  • The enabled state of channels is limited again by the current plan of this device. Channels beyond the allowance are shown as Disabled after the restore. For the allowances, see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.
  • This backup couldn't be read. Back up again to replace it. means that the backup is damaged, or that it was created by an older app with a PIN. Back up again on the original device; the new backup replaces the old one.
  • No backup available to restore. and Restore failed. Please try again. mean that no readable backup exists, or that the restore failed. Check that iCloud is signed in and synced, then try again.

Deleting the iCloud backup

  1. Tap the Settings tab, then tap Delete iCloud Backup in the Reset section.

    Check: The dialog Delete iCloud backup? appears and explains that the encrypted backup is removed from iCloud permanently. While no backup exists, the row is unavailable.

  2. Tap Delete iCloud Backup in the dialog.

    Check: The dialog closes and the row Delete iCloud Backup becomes unavailable.

  • On an iPhone or iPad this action deletes every copy in iCloud: the My Backup copy and the separate copy made for Apple TV. The same row on an Apple TV deletes only the copy made for Apple TV. The row is unavailable while no backup exists.
  • Other devices signed in with the same Apple Account lose this backup when they next sync. The devices and settings on this device are not affected.
  • When iCloud is not signed in, the action clears only the copy on this device, and the backup in the cloud can remain until the sign-in.

Moving devices and walls to a new phone

The LiveView Mix wall and its control panels belong to the app settings. Both methods below carry them: an iCloud backup always includes them, and a sharing code needs Include app settings to be on.

Method 1: moving with an iCloud backup (recommended)

Prerequisite: Cam Hub is installed on the new phone, which is signed in to iCloud with the same Apple Account.

  1. On the old phone, open the Settings tab and tap Back Up to iCloud.

    Check: The iCloud Backup page opens.

  2. Make sure Destination is My Backup and tap Back Up Now.

    Check: The page shows the green success message, and Last backed up shows the current time.

  3. On the new phone, open Cam Hub, tap the Settings tab, then tap Restore from iCloud.

    Check: The Restore from iCloud page opens. With Source set to My Backup, the iCloud Backup section shows the time and the number of devices of the backup of the old phone. When it has not synced yet, open the page again a little later.

  4. Tap Restore.

    Check: The page shows Restored 5 devices. The LiveView Mix tab shows the wall of the old phone.

  5. On the new phone, tap Restore Purchases in the Settings tab.

    Check: Purchases restored. appears. The plan is not part of the backup and is retrieved this way; see “Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code”.

Method 2: moving with a sharing code

  1. On the old phone, open the Settings tab and tap Export Cameras.

    Check: The Export Cameras page opens, with every device ticked by default.

  2. Turn on Include app settings.

    Check: The switch is on, and the LiveView Mix wall and the control panels travel with the code.

  3. Optional: set a PIN or a password as described in “Locking a code”.

    Check: The export button becomes available once the entry is complete.

  4. Tap the export button, then tap Share and send the link to the new phone.

    Check: The system share sheet has sent the link. Send the PIN or the password by another channel.

  5. On the new phone, tap the received link, tap Import Cameras and, for a locked code, enter the PIN or the password.

    Check: The screen shows Added 5 cameras. The LiveView Mix tab shows the wall of the old phone.

Neither method carries the plan. After signing in with the same Apple Account, retrieve it on the new phone with Restore Purchases; see “Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code”.

Bringing the setup to Apple TV

Apple TV neither creates nor edits walls, and entering a long code with the remote is laborious. The recommended approach is to finish the setup on an iPhone or iPad first. A backup made with Apple TV as the destination (see “Backing up to iCloud”) or a sharing code (see “Exporting cameras (creating a code)”) then brings the devices and the wall to the television. The steps for the Apple TV, and what differs there, are described in Chapter 14, “Apple TV”.

11Plans and limits

Cam Hub comes with a free basic allowance. When more channels or recorders are needed at the same time, subscription plans extend it. All plans offer the same functions; they differ only in the number of camera channels and recorders that can be enabled at the same time.

The allowance of each plan

PlanBillingWhat can be used at the same time
FreeNoneAt most 2 enabled channels in the whole app, counting the channels of standalone cameras and of recorders together. At most 1 recorder, and its enabled channels must all be on that one recorder.
Cam Home — 8 camerasYearlyUp to 8 standalone cameras can be enabled.
Cam Plus — 16 camerasYearlyUp to 16 standalone cameras can be enabled.
Cam Max — unlimited camerasYearlyAny number of standalone cameras can be enabled.
NVR Starter — 2 recordersMonthly2 recorders can be connected, and every channel of these 2 can be used.
NVR Pro — 4 recordersMonthly4 recorders can be connected, and every channel of these 4 can be used.
NVR Max — unlimited recordersMonthlyAny number of recorders can be connected, and every channel can be used.

Camera plans limit the number of enabled channels of standalone cameras, which are cameras that are not behind a recorder. NVR plans count recorders, not channels: every channel of a recorder that the plan covers is unlocked. The cost of each plan is shown on the plans screen of the app.

How the two groups of plans combine

Camera plans and NVR plans are two independent groups of subscriptions. Both can be held at the same time, and each decides the allowance of its own side.

Plans heldStandalone cameras (enabled channels)Recorders
None (free)At most 2, counted together with the channels of recorders1 recorder; its enabled channels must be on that one recorder, and together with standalone cameras the total stays at 2
A camera plan onlyAccording to the plan: 8, 16 or unlimitedStill the free allowance: 1 recorder with at most 2 enabled channels, no longer counted together with standalone cameras
An NVR plan onlyStill the free allowance: at most 2According to the plan: 2, 4 or unlimited recorders, with every channel of these recorders usable
BothAccording to the camera planAccording to the NVR plan
  • The two sides are counted separately. Unlocking recorders does not raise the limit for standalone cameras, and a higher camera plan does not add recorders.
  • Within one group only one plan is active at a time. A higher plan replaces a lower plan; they do not add up.
  • When both groups are raised to unlimited, Cam Hub turns on every channel automatically, and the row Choose which cameras show is hidden because nothing is left to choose.

What uses allowance

ItemHow it is counted
Enabled channels of standalone camerasEach channel uses 1 camera allowance.
RecordersCounted by number. While a recorder is within the number that the plan covers, every channel of it can be used. Without an NVR plan, the free allowance applies: at most 2 enabled channels on 1 recorder.
Disabled channelsThey use no allowance and do not stream.
Control panelsEach control panel uses 1 camera allowance, the same as a standalone camera. A subscription to an NVR plan alone does not add to this allowance. Clock, label, picture and empty tiles use no allowance. See Chapter 9, “Control panels and webhooks”.
Tiles of LiveView MixThe number of tiles of a wall is not limited; what is limited is the channels that can stream. LiveView Mix cannot show more cameras than the allowance of the plan.

When the allowance is not sufficient, items are kept in this order: first standalone cameras (in the order in which their devices were added, then by channel number), then control panels, and last the channels of recorders. On the free plan, only the first 2 of these three kinds together are kept, so one control panel can displace one recorder channel. With an NVR plan, the first recorders in sequence keep all their channels, and the channels of the remaining recorders are locked.

When a recorder is added and the number allowed by the plan has been reached, the plans screen opens with the text Free includes 1 recorder. Add more with an NVR plan. and the recorder is not added.

Examples of combinations

The examples apply the rules above. A channel is one picture of a camera; the channels of recorders and of standalone cameras are counted separately according to the plan.

Plan heldEquipmentResult
Free1 recorder (16 channels)At most 2 channels can be enabled, and both must be on this recorder. When a second recorder is added, the Plans screen opens with the reason and the recorder is not added.
Free2 standalone cameras and 1 recorderThe standalone cameras and the recorder channels count together, at most 2. With both standalone cameras enabled, no recorder channel can be enabled; after one standalone camera is disabled, 1 recorder channel can be enabled, and the total is still 2.
Free5 standalone camerasOnly 2 can be enabled and the other 3 stay disabled. To switch to another camera, disable an enabled one first and then enable the wanted one; see “Choosing which cameras show”.
Cam Home — 8 cameras10 standalone camerasUp to 8 can be enabled. To use the other 2, disable 2 of the enabled cameras first.
Cam Home — 8 cameras8 standalone cameras and 1 recorder (16 channels)The recorder is not affected by a camera plan and keeps the free allowance: 1 recorder with at most 2 enabled channels. Its channels no longer count together with the standalone cameras, so up to 8 standalone cameras plus 2 recorder channels can be used at the same time.
NVR Starter — 2 recorders2 recorders (16 channels each) and 4 standalone camerasEvery channel of the 2 recorders (32 in all) can be used. The standalone cameras keep the free allowance: at most 2 can be enabled. When a third recorder is added, the Plans screen opens and the recorder is not added.
Cam Plus — 16 cameras and NVR Pro — 4 recorders4 recorders and 12 standalone camerasEverything can be used: every channel of the 4 recorders, plus 12 standalone cameras (the limit is 16, so 4 are still free).
Cam Home — 8 cameras7 standalone cameras and 1 control panelThe control panel uses 1 camera allowance, so 8 are used and the allowance is full. When another standalone camera is added, it cannot be enabled until one of the items is disabled.
Cam Max — unlimited cameras and NVR Max — unlimited recordersAny number of cameras and recordersEvery channel is enabled automatically and nothing needs to be chosen. The row Choose which cameras show is hidden.
A change from NVR Pro — 4 recorders to NVR Starter — 2 recorders4 recordersThe first 2 recorders keep every channel. The channels of the other 2 stop streaming, their tiles show Not in your plan and a lock, and the devices and settings are kept. After subscribing again or restoring purchases they work at once; see “When a plan ends or is reduced”.

Choosing which cameras show

Path: Settings › Choose which cameras show. When the allowance of the plan is smaller than the total number of channels of the devices, the user decides which channels use it. This page gathers the channels of all devices on one screen, with one switch per channel; for the steps, see “Choosing which cameras show”.

  • What it does: a switch controls whether a channel is enabled. A channel that is off does not stream and uses no allowance, and it can be turned on again at any time; a channel that is on uses allowance. The switches on this page are the same function as Enable and Disable after touching and holding a channel tile on the device page; see “Channel options (long press)”.
  • The Your plan section shows the limits of the current plan: Cameras is the number of channels of standalone cameras that can be enabled, and Recorders is the number of recorders whose channels can all be used; each is a number or Unlimited.
  • When the allowance is used up, turning a switch on is refused: the switch stays off, and the plans screen opens with the reason at the top, for example You've reached the Free plan's limit of 2 enabled cameras., On the Free plan, the cameras you show must all be on one recorder. or Unlock every channel with an NVR plan. Turning a switch off is always possible.
  • When it is offered: the item is available only while at least one of the two limits of the plan is in effect. When both groups of plans are raised to unlimited, every channel is turned on automatically and the item is hidden. While no device exists, the page shows No Devices.
  • To obtain more allowance, subscribe as described in “Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code”. Channels beyond the allowance show Not in your plan and a lock on the wall and on the device page; see “What a thumbnail shows”.

Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code

Prerequisite: this device is signed in with an Apple Account in the system settings, and purchases are permitted. A subscription follows the Apple Account and is shared across iPhone, iPad and Apple TV.

  1. Tap the Settings tab at the bottom of the screen, then tap Plans in the Subscription section.

    Check: The Plans page opens. Below the row Plans, the current plan is shown; without a subscription it reads Free.

  2. In the section Camera plans · billed yearly or NVR plans · billed monthly, find the plan to take and tap Subscribe on its card.

    Check: The system purchase confirmation appears. Each card shows the name of the plan, a short description and its cost; when the Apple Account is eligible, the length of a free trial is shown as well.

  3. Follow the prompts of the system screen to confirm the purchase with the Apple Account.

    Check: The card of the plan changes to Current Plan, and the allowance is updated immediately. The row Plans in the Settings tab shows the name of the plan.

  4. Tap Done in the top-right corner.

    Check: The plans page closes and the settings list is shown again.

  • A subscription renews automatically until the user cancels it. Camera plans are billed yearly, NVR plans monthly.
  • When a purchase is not completed, the page shows Purchase failed. Please try again. When the plans cannot be loaded, it shows Couldn't load plans. Check your connection and try again. The names and descriptions of the plans are supplied by the app itself, and the cost appears once the purchase service has answered.
  • Manage Subscription opens the system subscription page, where a plan can be canceled or changed and the renewal date can be seen.
  • While plans of both groups are held, the row Plans joins the names of the two plans with a plus sign.
  • The text at the top of the plans page states that every plan includes all functions, including live view, recording playback and the multi-camera wall; that video does not pass through a cloud and needs no account; and that the two limits are counted separately. At the bottom of the page are the links Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Restoring purchases

Use this on another device, after a reinstallation, or when a purchase is not reflected immediately.

  1. In the Subscription section of the Settings tab, tap Restore Purchases. The same button is at the bottom of the plans page.

    Check: The app synchronizes the purchase records with the system purchase service and shows a message.

  2. Read the message and dismiss it.

    Check: When purchases are found, the message reads Purchases restored. and the allowance is updated. When none are found, it reads No purchases to restore. After an error it reads Restore failed. Please try again. When the system sign-in screen is canceled, no message appears.

Redeeming a code

  1. In the Subscription section of the Settings tab, tap Redeem Code. The same button is at the bottom of the plans page.

    Check: The system screen for redeeming a code appears.

  2. Follow the prompts of the system screen to enter and redeem the code.

    Check: After a successful redemption, the plan and the allowance are updated. When they are not updated yet, synchronize with Restore Purchases.

On Apple TV, Manage Subscription and Redeem Code are not offered; they are used on an iPhone or an iPad. See Chapter 14, “Apple TV”.

When a plan ends or is reduced

  • Cam Hub checks the plan whenever the app returns to the foreground. When a subscription ends without renewal, or a lower plan takes its place, the allowance shrinks accordingly.
  • The enabled state of channels is not rewritten, and the devices, names, wall layouts and settings are all kept. Channels beyond the new allowance stop streaming, and their tiles show Not in your plan and a lock. Tapping such a tile opens the plans screen with the reason. A locked channel cannot be used for recording playback either.
  • The order in which items are kept is the one described in “What uses allowance”: standalone cameras first, then control panels, and last the channels of recorders. A locked control panel shows a lock, its title and Not in your plan, and its buttons are unavailable.
  • After subscribing again or restoring purchases, the locked channels stream again, and no device has to be added again.
  • When a backup is restored or a code is imported, channels beyond the current allowance are written as Disabled. Such channels must be turned on again, as described in “Choosing which cameras show”, once the allowance is sufficient. See Chapter 10, “Sharing and backup”.

12The Tools tab

The Tools tab contains the network scan for finding devices, the speedometer with compass, and a section that adds sample devices. The scan is described step by step in the chapter on adding a device; this chapter gives an overview of the tab and describes the speedometer.

What the Tools tab contains

Path: Tools tab at the bottom of the screen. The tab is a single list. The sections follow each other in the order below.

SectionContentsDetails
SubnetThe row This device with the own address of the iPhone or iPad, the address field of the range, the selector Range, the line that states what will be scanned, the button Use my subnet (only while the range differs from the own network) and the button Scan or Stop.“Finding devices with the network scan”
Found DevicesThe progress of the scan and the addresses that answered. A tap on a result opens the Add Device form with the address filled in.“Finding devices with the network scan”
SpeedometerThe row Speedometer, which opens the speedometer with compass. The section is offered depending on the region and the language setting of the device.“Speedometer and compass”
DemoThe button Add Demo Estate (App Review), which adds sample devices.Below on this page.

  1. Tap the Tools tab at the bottom of the screen.

    Check: The screen shows the sections of the tab, beginning with Subnet. The address field and the range are already filled in with the network of the device.

For the steps of a scan, see “Finding devices with the network scan”. The following points concern the behavior of the tab as a whole.

  • Stored range: the address and the range are stored. When the device joins another network, both fields are filled in again for the new network, unless the range was typed by hand; a range that was typed by hand is kept. The button Use my subnet hands the choice back to the app. Restore Default Settings forgets the stored range; see “Reset: defaults, delete all data, delete iCloud backup”.
  • While a scan runs: the address field and the range cannot be changed. Stop ends the scan. A running scan also ends when the screen is left.
  • No sign-in: the scan checks only whether connections to the ports can be made and reads the name that a device announces on its web port. It does not sign in to any device. A device is added only after the credentials have been entered in the Add Device form.
  • Local network access: the first scan can cause the system to ask whether Cam Hub may find devices on the local network. When the access is refused, the scan finds nothing and shows no error; see “Finding devices with the network scan”.

Adding sample devices

The section Demo is at the end of the tab. Its text states that the devices are meant for the review of the app and that everyday use does not need them. They can be used by anyone to try the app without equipment. The sample devices draw their own pictures and need no network and no sign-in.

  1. Scroll to the end of the Tools tab and tap Add Demo Estate (App Review).

    Check: The app adds five recorders and two cameras. Each recorder has three channels. The recorders are named Demo NVR 1 to Demo NVR 5, and the cameras Demo Camera 1 and Demo Camera 2.

  2. Tap the Devices tab.

    Check: The list shows the sample devices. Their channels are enabled only as far as the current plan allows; the other channels show Disabled; see “Plan limits and enabling channels”.

  • Added once: when the sample devices already exist, the button adds nothing.
  • Counted like real devices: the sample recorders count toward the number of recorders that the plan allows, and enabled sample channels use places of the plan. Delete the sample devices before a real recorder is added on the free plan; see “The device list”.
  • Follow the plan: the app sets the enabled state of the sample channels again whenever it starts and whenever the plan changes, so that they always show what the plan allows. A switch that was changed by hand on a sample channel is not kept.
  • Limited functions: sample devices have no recording playback, no camera control and no snapshot, and the device page cannot refresh their channel list.

Speedometer and compass

The speedometer shows the speed of the device and the direction in which it moves or points. The position comes from satellite positioning. Whether the Tools tab offers the speedometer depends on the region and the language setting of the device. When it is not offered, the Tools tab shows the other sections only.

Opening the speedometer and allowing location access

Prerequisite: the iPhone or iPad has a clear view of the sky. Indoors, the position can be delayed or missing.

  1. Tap the Tools tab, scroll to the section Speedometer and tap the row Speedometer.

    Check: The screen Speedometer opens. When Cam Hub has not been allowed to use the location before, a system dialog asks for permission.

  2. Tap Allow While Using App.

    Check: The screen shows Waiting for GPS… until the first position has been received. The message then disappears.

  3. Move with the device, for example in a vehicle.

    Check: The large number shows the speed, and the compass dial turns with the direction.

Reading the screen

ElementMeaning
Large numberThe speed in km/h, rounded to whole numbers. The number shows — until the first measurement. A device at rest shows 0.
km/h and the line with mphThe same speed in both units. Both are always shown. There is no setting for the unit. Before the first measurement, the line reads 0 mph.
Compass dialThe dial turns below a fixed pointer at the top. The direction in which the device moves or points is the one below the pointer. The ring has a tick every 5 degrees and the letters N, E, S and W.
Text in the middle of the dialThe name of the direction (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W or NW) and the heading in degrees, counted clockwise from north. The text shows – until a heading is available.

The heading comes from two sources. While the device moves at 8 km/h or faster, it is the direction of travel determined by satellite positioning. At lower speeds, it is the heading of the compass of the device. When no compass reading exists, the last direction of travel is shown.

Messages below the compass

MessageMeaning and action
Waiting for GPS… (grey)No position has been received yet. Wait a few seconds, or move to a place with a clear view of the sky.
Can't get a GPS fix. (orange)The position could not be determined. The message disappears as soon as a position arrives. When it remains, move to a place with a clear view of the sky, or leave the screen and open it again.
Location access is off. Turn it on in Settings to see your speed and heading. (orange), with the button Open SettingsCam Hub is not allowed to use the location. Allow it as described below.
No messageA position is known. Speed and heading are current.

Allowing location access afterwards

  1. Tap Open Settings below the orange message.

    Check: The system settings of Cam Hub open.

  2. Tap Location and select While Using the App.

    Check: The entry Location shows While Using the App.

  3. Return to Cam Hub, tap the back button of the speedometer and open the row Speedometer again.

    Check: The screen shows Waiting for GPS… and then the speed and the heading.

Announcing the speed by voice

The switch Announce speed at the bottom of the screen is on by default. Its text reads Says your speed aloud every 10 km/h, from 150 up to 450 km/h.

  1. Tap the row Announce speed.

    Check: The switch is off. No speed is announced. The choice is stored.

  2. Tap the row Announce speed again.

    Check: The switch is on. The voice announces speeds from now on.

  • What is said: only the number in km/h, without a unit. The voice speaks once each time the speed passes the next multiple of ten, from 150 up to 450. Nothing is said below 150 or while the speed falls.
  • No repetition: a number is not repeated while the speed fluctuates slightly around it. It is said again only after the speed has fallen clearly below it and then risen again.
  • Switching on at speed: when the voice is switched on at a high speed, numbers that have already been passed are not announced. The next multiple of ten is the first one.
  • Language of the voice: the voice follows the language of the app (Settings › Language). When the device has no voice for that language, the English voice is used.
  • Other audio: music or other audio that plays at the same time becomes quieter while a number is spoken and continues afterwards.
  • Backup and reset: the switch is not part of the backups, and Restore Default Settings does not change it.

Leaving the speedometer

  1. Tap the back button in the top-left corner.

    Check: The Tools tab is shown again. The use of the location and the announcements stop.

  • Screen stays on: while the speedometer is open, the device does not lock the screen automatically.
  • Location only while open: Cam Hub uses the location only while the screen is open, and only while the app is in use. The position is used for the display and is not stored.

Default quality

The two rows set whether a picture starts as SD (lighter) or HD (sharper). The text below the section advises that viewing one camera can use more resources for a sharper picture, that the capacity of the device matters when many cameras are viewed at once, and that SD and HD look almost the same when each tile is small.

RowUsed byDefault
Single cameraThe single-camera view, see “Snapshot, sound and quality”, and the close-up of a camera in a wall, see “The full-screen wall of a device”.HD
Multiple camerasThe Live tab and the Full Screen Wall, see “SD and HD on a wall”, and the thumbnails of the device page, see “The device page”.SD

LiveView Mix walls are not affected: each camera slot has its own quality; see “Choosing cameras and quality”. For all screens, see “SD and HD on device screens”.

  1. In the Settings tab, find the section Default quality.

    Check: Two rows show a selector with SD and HD. Without a change, HD is selected for Single camera and SD for Multiple cameras.

  2. In the row Multiple cameras, tap HD.

    Check: HD is selected. The thumbnails of the device page change to HD at once. The Live tab changes to HD at once as well, unless the quality button of the Live tab has been used since the app started.

  3. To return, tap SD in the same row.

    Check: SD is selected.

The quality can still be switched while viewing; that change is not stored, as the text below the section states.

Picture: black bars and edge-to-edge

Both rows decide how much of the screen the picture uses: one inside its tile, the other against the edges of the device.

  • Black bars (default Default): the starting mode for the handling of black bars. Default shows the whole picture with black bars where the shapes differ, Enlarge to fill enlarges the picture in proportion and cuts off its edges, and Stretch to fill stretches the picture and can distort it; see “The device page”. The setting is the starting mode of the device page, the Full Screen Wall, the single-camera view and the Live tab. The device page and the Full Screen Wall read it each time they open, the single-camera view applies it at once, and the Live tab reads it when the app starts. The change of mode on a screen is not stored. LiveView Mix has its own setting for each wall; see “Black bars, edge-to-edge video and the angle of the device”.
  • Edge-to-Edge Video (default on): while the switch is on, full-screen video reaches into the area of the Dynamic Island and the rounded corners. While it is off, the picture stays clear of them, with black bars. The switch applies to the Full Screen Wall, to the full-screen wall of LiveView Mix and to the single-camera view held sideways; see “Black bars, rotation and landscape”.

  1. In the section Picture, tap Black bars.

    Check: A menu lists Default, Enlarge to fill and Stretch to fill. The current choice is marked.

  2. Tap Enlarge to fill.

    Check: The row shows Enlarge to fill. From now on, the screens named above start with this mode.

  3. Tap the switch of Edge-to-Edge Video.

    Check: The switch is off. Full-screen video keeps clear of the Dynamic Island and the rounded corners. Tap the switch again to turn it on.

Hide offline cameras

The row has no section title. While the switch is on, cameras without a signal do not appear on the Live tab and on the Full Screen Wall. The device page still lists them, grayed out. The switch is off by default; the effect, the cameras that are hidden and the way hidden cameras return are described in “Hiding cameras without signal”.

  1. Tap the switch of Hide offline cameras.

    Check: The switch is on, and all cameras are checked again. Tap the switch again to turn it off.

Backup and sharing of cameras

Two sections move devices to another iPhone, iPad or Apple TV. A backup in iCloud serves the same Apple Account. A code serves any other device, with no iCloud, and can be given to another person.

RowWhat it doesDetails
Back Up to iCloudOpens iCloud Backup. A backup of the devices, their passwords and the app settings is stored in encrypted form in the private iCloud. A backup is made only when Back Up Now is tapped; nothing is backed up automatically.“Backing up to iCloud”
Restore from iCloudOpens Restore from iCloud. The devices of the backup are added to this device or updated, and the app settings of the backup are applied.“Restoring from iCloud”
Export CamerasOpens Export Cameras, which produces an encrypted code with the selected devices. The row is unavailable while no device exists.“Exporting cameras (creating a code)”
Import CamerasOpens Import Cameras, where a code is pasted to add its cameras.“Importing cameras”

The text below the sections reads Encrypt your cameras and credentials to your private iCloud, then restore on another iPhone, iPad, or Apple TV signed in to the same Apple Account. and Move your cameras to another iPhone, iPad, or someone else's Cam Hub as one encrypted code — no iCloud needed. The two ways are compared in “Comparing the two methods”.

Language

The section title and the row are always written in English, whatever language is selected, so that the row can still be found after switching to a language that is not readable. The default is Follow System, which uses the language setting of the iPhone or iPad.

  1. Tap the row Language.

    Check: A menu lists Follow System and the languages English, 繁體中文, 简体中文, 日本語, 한국어, العربية, Deutsch, Español and Français. Each language is written in its own name.

  2. Tap the language.

    Check: The whole app switches to the language at once. No restart is needed, and the screen stays on the Settings tab. For Arabic, the layout is mirrored from right to left; it returns to the usual direction when another language is selected.

The voice of the speedometer follows the language of the app; see “Speedometer and compass”.

Reset: defaults, delete all data, delete iCloud backup

The section Reset has three rows. Each one asks for a confirmation before it acts. The text below the section reads Restore settings keeps your devices. Delete all data also removes every device and saved password from this iPhone or iPad — your iCloud backup and subscription are kept.

RowRemovesKeeps
Restore Default SettingsThe settings listed in the table below, including the whole LiveView Mix wall.Devices, channels with their enabled state and names, saved passwords, iCloud backups, subscriptions.
Delete All DataEvery device with its channels, every saved password, the downloaded recording clips and the stored last pictures. Then everything that Restore Default Settings resets.iCloud backups and subscriptions.
Delete iCloud BackupEvery copy in iCloud: the backup My Backup and the separate copy for Apple TV. The row is unavailable while no backup exists.Everything on this device.
Restore Default Settings also deletes the LiveView Mix wall

The confirmation dialog states only that every setting returns to its default. In addition, the whole LiveView Mix wall is deleted: the selected cameras, the layouts, the slots with their clocks, labels and pictures, the control panels with their webhook buttons, and the watermark. The wall is not a device and is not kept. It can be brought back only from an iCloud backup made earlier, or from a code that was exported with Include app settings; see “What backups and codes contain”. Make a backup before the action when the wall is still needed.

Restoring the default settings

  1. In the section Reset, tap Restore Default Settings.

    Check: The dialog Restore all settings to defaults? appears, with the buttons Restore Defaults and Cancel. The text of the dialog states that the LiveView Mix wall (layouts, control panels, webhook buttons and pictures) is cleared and that the devices and the iCloud backup are kept.

  2. Tap Restore Defaults. Tap Cancel instead to keep everything as it is.

    Check: The settings show their defaults, and the language follows the system. The row LiveView Mix shows Not set up. The devices are still listed in the Devices tab.

Deleting all data

Use this action to empty the app, for example before the device is passed on. It cannot be undone. Without an iCloud backup or an export code, the passwords of the cameras cannot be recovered, because they are stored only on this device.

  1. In the section Reset, tap Delete All Data.

    Check: The dialog Delete all data? appears, with the buttons Delete Everything and Cancel. Its text depends on the iCloud backup. With a backup, it reads This removes every device, camera, and saved password from this device. Your iCloud backup and subscription are not affected. Without a backup, it reads There's no iCloud backup, so this can't be undone — camera passwords live only on this device and can't be recovered. Your subscription is not affected.

  2. Tap Delete Everything. Tap Cancel instead to keep the data.

    Check: The Devices tab shows No Devices, and the settings show their defaults. An iCloud backup that exists can be restored as described in “Restoring from iCloud”.

Deleting the iCloud backup

On an iPhone or iPad the action removes every copy in iCloud: the backup My Backup and the separate copy for Apple TV. The steps and the details are in “Deleting the iCloud backup”.

  1. In the section Reset, tap Delete iCloud Backup. The row is unavailable while no backup exists.

    Check: The dialog Delete iCloud backup? appears. It states that the encrypted backup is removed from iCloud permanently, that other devices signed in with the same Apple Account lose it when they next sync, and that the devices and settings on this device are not affected.

  2. Tap Delete iCloud Backup in the dialog.

    Check: The dialog closes, and the row Delete iCloud Backup becomes unavailable.

Terms of Use and Privacy Policy

The two rows in the section Legal open the pages of the website in the browser, outside the app. An internet connection is required. The pages are the same ones that are shown before a subscription is taken, and the same links are at the bottom of the plans page.

  1. In the section Legal, tap Terms of Use or Privacy Policy.

    Check: The browser opens the page https://cam-hub.almx.cc/terms.html or https://cam-hub.almx.cc/privacy.html. Return to Cam Hub with the app switcher of the device.

About and what Settings does not contain

  1. Scroll to the end of the Settings tab.

    Check: The section About has one row, Version. It shows the version number of the installed app, followed by a second number in parentheses. The row is for information and opens nothing.

  • Appearance: the app always uses a dark appearance. There is no setting for it.
  • Sound: sound is not switched in Settings but with the speaker button of the single-camera view; see “Snapshot, sound and quality”.
  • Names of devices and channels: they are changed on the device page, not in Settings; see “The device page”.
  • Notifications: Cam Hub shows no notifications and has no setting for them.

14Apple TV

The Apple TV app shows the devices and the LiveView Mix wall that were set up on an iPhone or an iPad. The recommended order is to finish the whole setup on an iPhone or iPad first and to bring it to the Apple TV afterwards. This chapter gives the steps for that and lists what differs on the television. It is not an operating guide for the Apple TV app.

Set up on an iPhone or iPad first

The Apple TV is operated with a remote. Typing, drawing and choosing are laborious there, and several functions are not offered at all. These tasks are therefore done on an iPhone or an iPad before the Apple TV is used:

  • Adding the devices; see Chapter 3, “Adding a device”.
  • Building the LiveView Mix wall, with a custom layout and control panels where wanted; see Chapter 8, “LiveView Mix” and Chapter 9, “Control panels and webhooks”.
  • Choosing the plans and the cameras that show; see Chapter 11, “Plans and limits”.

Bringing the setup to the Apple TV

Prerequisites: the iPhone or iPad and the Apple TV are signed in to iCloud with the same Apple Account, and both run the same version of Cam Hub. A backup that an older version made does not appear on the Apple TV.

  1. On the iPhone or iPad, finish the setup: the devices, the LiveView Mix wall, the plans and the choice of cameras that show.

    Check: The devices and the wall appear on the iPhone or iPad the way they are to appear on the television.

  2. On the iPhone or iPad, back up to iCloud with Apple TV as the destination; see “Backing up to iCloud”.

    Check: The backup page shows the message that the backup was made, and Current Backup shows the time and the number of devices.

  3. On the Apple TV, restore the backup in the Settings tab, under iCloud Backup › Restore from iCloud. What a restore changes is described in “Restoring from iCloud”.

    Check: The Devices tab of the Apple TV lists the restored devices, and the LiveView Mix tab shows the wall. When the Apple TV reports that no backup was found, see “Sharing, import and iCloud backup”.

  4. On the Apple TV, select Plans in the Settings tab.

    Check: The page shows the plan of the Apple Account. A plan that is not shown yet appears after Restore Purchases.

When the two devices do not share an Apple Account, a sharing code replaces the backup. Create the code on the iPhone or iPad as described in “Exporting cameras (creating a code)” and copy it. On the Apple TV, select Share Cameras › Import Cameras in the Settings tab and enter the code; when the keyboard appears, a nearby iPhone can type it. A locked code asks for its PIN or password. A code can be hundreds to thousands of characters long, so an iCloud backup is preferable whenever the Apple Account is the same.

Later changes reach the Apple TV only with a new backup

After devices, the wall or the plans have been changed on the iPhone or iPad, repeat steps 2 and 3. The Apple TV does not follow changes by itself.

What differs on the Apple TV

AreaiPhone and iPadApple TV

OperationTouch, with gestures such as pinch, drag and long press.Remote. The selection moves with the directional pad or by swiping, Select acts like a tap and Menu goes back. There are no touch gestures.
Adding devicesA form with ports, a list of brands, the network scan, the checklist and the device report.A short form with name, address, username, password and the switch Connect via ONVIF, opened with Add IP Device. The ports are fixed at 80 and 554. There is no scan, no list of brands, no checklist and no device report. At the recorder limit, only Something went wrong. Please try again. is shown, without the plans screen.
Device pageA menu for each camera: rename, enable or disable, pause. A device is deleted from the list.The device can be renamed and deleted, and its details shown or hidden. There is no menu for a camera. Channels are switched on and off in Settings › Choose which cameras show.
Live view and single cameraSD and HD, sound, snapshot, PTZ, pinch zoom, landscape view.SD and HD, sound, and a choice between fitting the picture and filling the screen. There is no snapshot, no PTZ and no pinch zoom.
Recording playbackCalendar for the day, a timeline that is dragged, speeds of 2×, 4× and 8×, search for people.Available for devices that support playback. A bar is moved with the remote, with buttons for the previous and the next day and for zooming the bar, and a list of detected people where the device offers one. There is no calendar and no faster speed. A recording that has to be downloaded first is not played; the screen refers to the iPhone or iPad.
LiveView MixChoosing cameras, arranging, drawing layouts, editing slots, watermark, keeping cameras connected.The wall is shown and operated with the remote. A reduced editor in Settings › LiveView Mix offers the choice of cameras with SD or HD, a ready-made layout and black bars. Ready-made layouts of more than 16 tiles are offered only there. A custom layout that was drawn on an iPhone or iPad is shown but cannot be edited. Control panels can be pressed but not edited. Arranging, slot editing, the watermark and keeping cameras connected are not offered.
Backup and sharingCreating a backup, restoring, exporting a code, importing a code.Restoring the Apple TV copy of a backup and importing a typed code. A backup or a code cannot be created.
PlansPlans, Manage Subscription, Restore Purchases and Redeem Code.Plans and Restore Purchases. There is no Manage Subscription and no Redeem Code. One subscription covers every device that uses the same Apple Account.
PermissionsLocal Network; Camera for Take Photo; Location for the Speedometer.Local Network only; see “Permission requests and system dialogs”.

The settings for the language, the default quality, Hide offline cameras and the legal pages are available on the Apple TV as well. Problems with a backup that does not appear on the Apple TV are covered in “Sharing, import and iCloud backup”.

15Troubleshooting

This chapter lists, by symptom, what the empty screens, messages, permission requests and notices of Cam Hub mean, the likely cause and what to do. Connection failures while adding a device are covered in “When adding fails: the checklist” and are not repeated here.

Where to start

Most connection symptoms trace back to one of four causes. Check them in this order before reading the sections below.

  1. The iPhone or iPad is on the same Wi-Fi network as the device. A guest network, a separate VLAN, client isolation on the router and a VPN on the phone all block the connection.
  2. Cam Hub is allowed to use the local network; see “Permission requests and system dialogs”.
  3. The device is powered on and still has the address that was entered in Cam Hub. After a restart, a router can assign a different address to a device; a fixed address prevents this.
  4. The account and the password are still valid on the device. After several wrong attempts, a device can lock the account for a while.
SymptomWhere to look
A device cannot be added, or its connection indicator is red“When adding fails: the checklist”, “A device is added, but it is not reachable”
A screen is empty and shows only a title and a sentence“What the empty screens say”
A camera shows no picture, a black picture, an error message or no sound“Live view”
The list of recordings is empty, the times differ, or playback does not speed up“Recording playback”
A tile of the LiveView Mix wall shows a status text, or the wall has changed“LiveView Mix”
A control panel button shows an orange triangle“Control panels and webhooks”
A code or a backup cannot be imported or restored“Sharing, import and iCloud backup”
A lock, the plans screen or a plan message appears unexpectedly“Plans and purchases”
A message sentence is not listed above“Other error sentences”
The system asks for permission, or a permission was refused“Permission requests and system dialogs”
None of the above applies“Reaching the developer”, “Questions and answers”

An empty screen is not an error. It states that nothing has been set up yet, or that nothing can be drawn for the current settings.

A device is added, but it is not reachable

The checklist after a failed attempt and the device report are described in “When adding fails: the checklist” and “Device report (experimental)”. The symptoms below appear after a device has been added.

What is shownLikely causeWhat to do
A red, crossed-out Wi-Fi symbol in the device listThe device did not accept a connection on its HTTP port within about 4 seconds. It may be switched off, on another network, or blocked by a firewall. A device that was added through a brand from the list, or one that uses another port for video, can show the red symbol while its video works.Check the power and the network. When the video plays, the symbol can be ignored. See “The device list”.
A device that worked yesterday is unreachable todayThe address of the device changed. A device keeps the address with which it was added.Look up the new address on the router, delete the old device and add the device again with the new address; see “The Add Device form”. A fixed address in the device or in the router prevents a repetition.
A saved password no longer worksThe password was changed on the device.Add the device again with the same address, HTTP port and username; the device and its stored password are updated in place. See “The Add Device form”.
