A device cannot be added at all, and it only works in the app of its makerThe device offers no connection on the local network, or it accepts HTTPS only.See “Requirements and limits”.

Live view

What is shownLikely causeWhat to do
A grey tile with a crossed-out camera and No signalThe device reports that this channel has no video signal. The camera behind the channel is off, disconnected from the recorder, or has lost its network link.Check the power and the cable or network of the camera. When it is back, open the device page, or pull down on it, to read the channel list again. When a camera is missing from the Live tab altogether, check whether Hide offline cameras is on; see “Hiding cameras without signal”.
A message with a warning symbol and the button RetryThe stream could not be opened. The message names the cause, with the same wording as when a device is added.Find the sentence in “When adding fails: the checklist” or “Other error sentences”, correct the cause, then tap Retry.
Wrong username or password. for a device that worked beforeThe password was changed on the device, or the account was locked or removed. Cam Hub does not try again by itself after this message.Correct the account on the device, or wait until a lock ends, usually about 30 minutes. To store a new password, add the device again with the same address, HTTP port and username.
Connecting… for a long time, or Reconnecting… again and againThe network is weak, or the device does not answer. Cam Hub tries again at growing intervals of up to about 15 seconds. A stream that delivers nothing for 15 seconds is treated as interrupted. A device can also serve only a limited number of viewers at the same time.Check the Wi-Fi signal. Close other viewers of the same camera. In a wall with many cameras, use SD instead of HD; see “SD and HD on device screens”.
A black picture without a messageThe camera sends a video format that the phone cannot decode. Cam Hub plays H.264 and H.265 only. An iPhone without hardware support for H.265, or a picture size above the limit of the decoder, shows no picture.In the stream settings of the camera, select H.264 and a lower resolution. A key frame interval of one to two seconds helps when the picture appears only after a long delay. See “Connection states and messages”.
The picture is blurred or blockyThe wall or the view uses SD, or the device offers only one stream. SD and HD are the same stream for some devices.Switch to HD in the single-camera view. Default values are set in the Settings tab; see “SD and HD on device screens”.
No speaker button, or no soundSound is off until the speaker button is tapped. The button appears only when the stream carries sound in a supported format (G.711 or AAC-LC). Sound plays only in the single-camera view and in the close-up of a wall, never on wall tiles and never in the background. Playback faster than 1× is muted.Tap the speaker button. When it is missing, the stream has no usable sound; turn on a supported audio format in the settings of the camera. Cam Hub only listens; there is no talk-back.
Paused, Disabled or Not in your planThe channel was paused, was not enabled, or is beyond the allowance of the plan.See “What a thumbnail shows” and “Plans and purchases”.
Pictures stop when the app is left or the phone is lockedThis is intended. Every stream stops in the background and connects again when the app returns.No action is needed. A recording that was playing resumes where it stopped.

Unlock every channel with an NVR plan.The channel belongs to a recorder that the plan does not cover.Subscribe to an NVR plan, or turn off the channels that are not needed.
A tile shows Not in your plan and a lockThe channel is enabled, but the allowance covers fewer channels than are enabled.Tap the tile to see the reason, free an allowance as in “Choosing which cameras show”, or subscribe. The order in which channels are kept is in “What uses allowance”.
Locked — upgrade to enable with the button PlansThe channel left the plan while the view was open, for example because a subscription ended.Tap Plans; see “When a plan ends or is reduced”.
After a new installation or on a new device, no plan is shownThe plan is tied to the Apple Account, not to the app. It has to be fetched again.Sign in with the same Apple Account in the system settings, then tap Restore Purchases. Purchases restored. confirms it, and No purchases to restore. means that the Apple Account holds none.
Couldn't load plans. Check your connection and try again.The App Store did not answer.Check the internet connection and open the plans page again.
Purchase failed. Please try again.The purchase did not complete, for example because the payment method of the Apple Account was refused.Check the payment settings of the Apple Account in the system settings and try again.
A subscription has to be canceled or changedSubscriptions are managed by Apple.Tap Manage Subscription. Charges, renewals and refunds are handled by Apple, not by the developer of Cam Hub.

Other error sentences

These sentences appear in the failure message over a picture, above the timeline of the recordings panel and in the add-device form. The first four are explained with the checks in “When adding fails: the checklist”.

SentenceMeaningWhat to do
Device unreachable. Check the address and your network.No answer from the device.See “When adding fails: the checklist” and “Where to start”.
Wrong username or password.The device refused the sign-in.See “When adding fails: the checklist”.
Not a supported device.The device answers, but not in a way that Cam Hub recognizes with the connection method in use.Try another connection method; see “Connection methods”.
This camera is offline.The channel has no signal.See “Live view”.
Could not connect to the video stream.The connection to the video port failed or timed out.Check that RTSP is switched on and that the RTSP port is correct (usually 554).
The device refused the video stream (HTTP 404).The device answered the video request with a status other than a sign-in refusal. The number is the status of the device.Check the account rights for live view, the stream settings and the number of viewers of the device.
The recorder answered with HTTP 500.The recorder answered a request with an error status.Try again later, restart the recorder if needed, and check its firmware.
The device sent an unexpected reply.The device answered in a form that Cam Hub cannot read.Try again. When it persists, note the model and the firmware version and contact the developer; see “Reaching the developer”.
Surveillance Station refused the request.The network storage device refused the request of the account.Check that the account is allowed to use the recording software of the network storage device. Cam Hub has no field for a verification code, so an account that requires two-step verification cannot be used.
The connection timed out.The device took too long to answer.Check the network, then try again.
No internet connection. or Could not reach the server.The phone has no internet connection, or the server cannot be reached.Check the mobile data or Wi-Fi connection of the phone, then try again.
Something went wrong. Please try again.An unexpected error. When a device is added through a brand from the list, the same sentence also stands for an unreachable device.Try again, and work through “When adding fails: the checklist”.

Some messages come from the video stream itself and are shown in English whatever the language of the app, for example Wrong username or password without a full stop, Connection closed or HTTP 404. They have the same meaning as the sentences above.

Permission requests and system dialogs

Cam Hub asks for as few permissions as possible. It never asks for access to the microphone, the photo library, notifications, contacts or Bluetooth, and it sends no notifications.

RequestWhen it appearsWhat to know
Local NetworkThe first time the app contacts an address on the local network: when a device is added, when the connection indicator of the list checks a device, when a scan runs, or when a stream starts. The text reads “Cam Hub connects to cameras and recorders and scans a subnet you choose to find equipment on your local network.”Allow it; without it, no device on the home network can be reached. When it was refused, adding a device fails with Device unreachable. Check the address and your network., pictures do not load, and a scan finds nothing without any message. The procedure below turns the permission on.
CameraOnly when Take Photo is chosen for a picture in an empty slot of LiveView Mix. The text reads “Cam Hub uses the camera only when you choose Take Photo for a LiveView Mix slot.”When it was refused, use Choose Photo instead. Camera access can be changed in the system settings.
PhotosNot requested. Choose Photo uses the system picker, and a snapshot is passed on through the share sheet.Cam Hub never writes to the photo library by itself. Save a snapshot from the share sheet.
Location, while in useThe first time the Speedometer of the Tools tab opens; see “Speedometer and compass”.It is used only for the speed and the compass heading, and is neither stored nor shared. There is no access in the background. When it is refused, the Speedometer shows an orange line and the button Open Settings.
iCloudNo request. Backup and restore need a device that is signed in to iCloud with an Apple Account.When backup fails, see “Sharing, import and iCloud backup”.
Purchases, Manage Subscription and Redeem CodeSystem sheets of the App Store, opened from the Settings tab or from the plans page.Confirm with the Apple Account. See “Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code”.
Share linksA link of the form https://cam-hub.almx.cc/i#… opens the import page of Cam Hub with the code already entered.The code is in the part of the address after the #, which is not sent to a server. See “Importing cameras”.
MailEmail to developer in the device report opens the mail composer of the system, addressed to the developer.Nothing is sent until Send is tapped in the composer. Without a mail account, the screen shows Mail isn't set up on this device; the report is copied and stays on the device, and the copy expires after about 2 minutes. See “Device report (experimental)”.
Rating requestThe system may ask for a rating after a successful backup.The request can be dismissed.

Turning on the Local Network permission after it was refused:

  1. Open the system Settings app and tap Privacy & Security.

    Check: The list of privacy categories is shown.

  2. Tap Local Network.

    Check: The list of apps that asked for local network access is shown, each with a switch.

  3. Switch on Cam Hub.

    Check: The switch next to Cam Hub is on.

  4. Return to Cam Hub and repeat the action that failed.

    Check: The device is reached, or the scan lists devices.

Reaching the developer

The settings of the app have no support row. The developer can be reached in three ways:

  • Support page: support.html on the website of Cam Hub. It holds notes on compatibility, a list of checks before a connection problem is reported, and the contact address.
  • Email: app-dev@almx.cc. This is the address to which the mail composer of the device report is already addressed.
  • Device report: after a failed attempt to add a device, the experimental report collects technical details and offers to email them; see “Device report (experimental)”.

A message helps the developer most when it states:

  • the version of the app, shown in Settings › About › Version;
  • the model of the iPhone or iPad and the version of its system;
  • the brand and model of the camera or recorder, and the version of its firmware;
  • the connection method that was used;
  • the exact message that the screen showed, and what was tried before.
Never send these items

The password of a camera, the PIN or password of a sharing code, a complete sharing code, and the public address with which a device is reached over the internet. The developer never needs them.

A device that cannot be supported by design, for example one that works only through the cloud app of its maker, cannot be fixed by a message; see “Requirements and limits”. Questions about charges and refunds go to Apple.

Questions and answers

Why does the app always open on the LiveView Mix tab?

The app always opens on the first tab. In Settings › Open on launch, the Live tab of a chosen device, or the full-screen LiveView Mix wall, can open instead. The choice Last viewed does not restore the last tab. See “LiveView Mix in Settings”.

Why is the app always dark?

Cam Hub has one appearance, and the settings contain no row for it.

Why are there no notifications for motion or alarms?

Cam Hub is a viewer. It sends no push notifications and no local notifications, and it asks for no permission for them.

Can cameras be watched from outside the home?

Cam Hub connects directly to the devices and uses no cloud service of its own. A device outside the home network can be reached only with an address that is reachable from the internet, or through a VPN back to the home network. A private VPN is the safer way, because it keeps the device off the open internet.

Can a recording be saved or exported?

No. Recordings can only be watched. A snapshot is a still image that the device supplies at the moment of the tap; during playback it shows the current live picture. See “What is not available”.

Why is there no sound?

Sound is off until the speaker button is tapped, and the button appears only when the stream carries sound in a supported format. Cam Hub only listens; two-way audio is not offered. See “Live view”.

Why does SD look like HD?

Some devices serve one stream for every channel. SD and HD then show the same picture. Devices added through a brand from the list usually behave this way. See “What works with which method”.

Why do the times of the recordings differ from the clock of the phone?

The times belong to the clock of the device and are never converted. Correct the date, the time and the time zone on the device; see “While a recording plays”.

A camera works in the app of its maker, but not in Cam Hub. What helps?

Try another connection method (ONVIF or a brand from the list), switch on ONVIF and RTSP on the device, create a separate ONVIF user where the device has its own list, and check the video format. Devices that need the cloud of their maker cannot be added. See “Requirements and limits”.

Can a device that accepts only HTTPS be added?

No. Cam Hub controls devices over plain HTTP. A device with HTTP switched off cannot be added. For network storage devices, the port of the HTTP web interface is entered, not the port of the HTTPS one. See “Requirements and limits”.

How are the address or the password of a saved device changed?

A saved device has no edit screen. For a new password, add the device again with the same address, HTTP port and username; the stored device is updated. A new address creates a new device, so delete the old one first. See “The Add Device form”.

How many cameras can be watched without a plan?

Two enabled channels in the whole app, and one recorder. See “The allowance of each plan”.

Does a plan apply to all devices that use the same Apple Account?

Yes, on every iPhone, iPad and Apple TV that is signed in with the same Apple Account. On a new device, tap Restore Purchases. See “Subscribing, restoring purchases and redeeming a code”.

All data was deleted. Can the cameras be recovered?

Only from an iCloud backup that was made before, with Restore from iCloud; see “Restoring from iCloud”. Without such a backup, the passwords of the cameras cannot be recovered, because they are stored only on the device where they were entered. Plans are not affected by Delete All Data.

Does the device report send the password?

No. The password is never part of the report, and nothing is sent unless the person chooses to email it. See “Device report (experimental)”.

Why does the screen not turn off?

While a live picture or a recording is on the screen, the app keeps the screen awake. Leaving the video, or leaving the app, ends this.

Why does the picture stop when another app is opened?

Every stream stops when the app leaves the foreground, and sound never plays in the background. When the app returns, the streams connect again.

16Supported brands and connection methods

This is the only chapter that names brands. It lists the connection methods of the add-device form, what each one makes possible, what a device must offer, and what to prepare on a device before it is added. Everything else in this manual describes functions without naming a brand.

Connection methods

The menu Connect using in the add-device form offers eleven choices: Auto-detect, ONVIF and nine brand names. The form itself is described in “The Add Device form” and the choice in “Choosing the connection method”.

ChoiceWhat Cam Hub doesSuitable forAccount
Auto-detect (default) Tries, in this order, the protocol of Hikvision, the protocol of Dahua, the programming interface of Synology Surveillance Station, and ONVIF, and keeps the first one that recognizes the device. It moves on to the next only when a device answers that it is not of that kind. A device that cannot be reached, or a refused sign-in, ends the attempt at once. The HTTP port field is used for all control requests, and the RTSP port field for video. Cameras and recorders of the three named families, and any other device that offers ONVIF. The account of the device. For Synology: an account of the network storage device that may use Surveillance Station.
ONVIF Skips the detection and uses only the open ONVIF protocol. The HTTP port field has to hold the ONVIF port, because the service is expected at /onvif/device_service on that port. The video is fetched at the address that the device announces. Any camera or recorder with ONVIF; also a device of the three named families that is to be used over ONVIF. The ONVIF user of the device. Where the device keeps a separate list of ONVIF users, a user has to exist in that list.
One of nine brand names (see “The nine RTSP-only brands”) Connects over plain RTSP, at the stream paths that the maker documents. No control interface of the device is contacted. Live view only. Devices of that brand when ONVIF is switched off, or when ONVIF does not work. The camera account of the device; for two of the brands a separate account.

Auto-detect is the starting point. ONVIF is the next choice when Auto-detect reports Not a supported device., or when a device is to be used over ONVIF on purpose. A brand name is the last choice, for a device with ONVIF switched off. The developer has tested selected devices of the three named families. Whether a particular model works, with any method, depends on its firmware, its settings, its stream format, its account rights and the network.

What works with which method

The table shows what Cam Hub offers for each method. Yes means that the function is offered. If supported means that the function appears only when the device itself offers it. No means that Cam Hub does not offer the function with this method. The notes below the table give the details.

FunctionHikvisionDahuaSynology Surveillance StationONVIFNine RTSP-only brands
Live viewYesYesYesIf supportedYes
SD and HDYesYesHiddenIf supportedShown, usually one stream
Recording playbackYesNoYesIf supportedNo
Playback speed 2×, 4×, 8×If supportedNoNoIf supportedNo
Search for peopleIf supportedNoNoNoNo
PTZIf supportedIf supportedIf supportedIf supportedNo
SnapshotYesYesYesIf supportedNo
Sound (listening)If supportedIf supportedIf supportedIf supportedIf supported
Channel listFor recordersFor recordersYesYesTyped number
  • Live view: with ONVIF, the device must announce a stream address.
  • SD and HD: with Synology Surveillance Station, the choice is hidden, and SD uses the low-resolution stream of a camera that has one. With ONVIF, the largest profile of the device is HD and the smallest is SD, and a single profile serves both. With the nine RTSP-only brands, the choice is shown, but SD and HD are normally the same stream.
  • Recording playback: with Hikvision, a camera with its own storage plays back like a recorder. With Synology Surveillance Station, the recording is streamed and can be moved within. With ONVIF, the device needs the search and replay services that ONVIF defines for playback.
  • Playback speed: with Hikvision and ONVIF, the recorder may refuse a faster speed. With Synology Surveillance Station, streamed playback has no speed button.
  • Search for people: the recorder needs an index of detected people.
  • PTZ: with Hikvision, a channel needs PTZ switched on; saved positions appear when the device lists them, and the home position is always available. With Dahua, PTZ must be bound to that channel; saved positions are offered, but there is no home position. With Synology Surveillance Station, the controls follow what the system reports for the camera: four directions, and the home position when it is reported. With ONVIF, the axes follow what the device reports; a camera with zoom only gets no direction pad.
  • Snapshot: with ONVIF, the device must give a snapshot address.
  • Sound: with Synology Surveillance Station, only G.711 plays over its usual streaming path.
  • Channel list: Hikvision and Dahua list the channels of a recorder with names and signal state, and a device that is not a recorder has one channel. Synology Surveillance Station lists every camera of the system as a channel with its signal state. ONVIF lists one channel for each separate video source and does not report a signal state. The RTSP-only brands have no list: the number of cameras is entered (1 to 64), and every channel is shown as online.

Not available with any method: talk-back (two-way audio), focus and iris control, saving or exporting recordings, logging in to a cloud account, and a connection over HTTPS.

The nine RTSP-only brands

These brands are connected over plain RTSP. In the add-device form, a brand name adds the field Cameras (1 to 64) and a path field. With 1, the device is added as a camera that is named after the brand; with a larger number, it is added as a recorder with channels CH1 to CHn, and it counts as a recorder for the plan. A blank path field makes Cam Hub try the documented paths in turn and keep the one that the device answers. Only a particular path needs to be entered.

Brand in the menuDevicesRecorder formNotes
AxisCamerasNoNeeds its own camera or ONVIF account, created in the web interface or the app of the maker; the administrator login alone may be refused. The device offers a single stream path, so SD differs from HD only by a resolution parameter.
Hanwha Vision (Wisenet)Cameras and recordersYesThe second profile is the usual main stream. The first profile of some models sends MJPEG, which cannot be played. The profile that serves as SD is a best effort.
Uniview (UNV)Cameras and recordersYesThe stream index of a recorder starts at 0 while channels start at 1; Cam Hub takes care of this.
VIVOTEKCameras and recordersYesOlder firmware uses other paths than newer firmware. Both are tried.
i-PRO (Panasonic)CamerasNoOne path for the main stream and one for the second stream.
Bosch SecurityCameras and encoders of one product lineNoRecorders of this brand are not covered. Some paths vary by model or firmware, so the first attempt may not match.
AvigilonCamerasNoThe path of the second stream is an estimate. Some paths vary by model or firmware. The RTSP port can be changed on the device.
PelcoCameras and encodersYes (encoders)Two firmware families use different paths. Both are tried. Some paths vary by model or firmware.
TP-Link (Tapo / VIGI)Tapo cameras, VIGI cameras, VIGI recordersYesNeeds its own camera account, created in the Tapo app, before RTSP works. The administrator login alone may be refused.

These paths follow the documentation of each maker. They have not been tested on real devices, and they have not been verified on every model. Results depend on the model and the firmware. A device with ONVIF switched on is better connected with ONVIF, because Cam Hub then asks the device for its stream address instead of trying paths.

Live view only

A connection through one of these brands has no recording playback, no PTZ control, no snapshot and no channel list. The functions are listed in “What works with which method”.

Requirements and limits

TopicRequirement or limit
Plain HTTP onlyCam Hub contacts every device over plain HTTP, and fetches video over RTSP on TCP. HTTPS and self-signed certificates are not supported for devices. A device with HTTP switched off, or one that accepts HTTPS only, cannot be added. For a network storage device, enter the port of its HTTP web interface, for example 5000, not the port of the HTTPS interface.
ONVIF switched onFor the choice ONVIF, ONVIF must be switched on at the device. Cam Hub expects the service at /onvif/device_service on the port entered in HTTP Port. Some devices have ONVIF switched off in the factory settings.
RTSP switched onVideo is fetched over RTSP, on the port entered in RTSP Port (usually 554). A network storage device may use its own streaming path first. Where the device has a setting for RTSP authentication, Digest is the method to select.
A separate ONVIF userSome devices keep a list of ONVIF users that is separate from the users of the web interface, and the administrator login does not work for ONVIF. Create a user in that list. Two brands in the menu need their own camera or ONVIF account before RTSP works: Axis and TP-Link (Tapo / VIGI).
Account rightsThe account needs the right to view live video, and for playback the right to read recordings. For Synology, the account must be allowed to use Surveillance Station. Cam Hub has no field for a verification code, so an account that requires two-step verification cannot be used.
Clock of the deviceThe ONVIF sign-in carries a time stamp of the device. A clock that is minutes off makes the sign-in fail. Set the time on the device, for example with network time. The times of recordings are the clock of the recorder.
Same network, no cloudCam Hub connects directly to the address of the device and has no cloud relay. From outside the home network, a device can be reached only through an address that is reachable from the internet, or through a VPN. Devices that work only through the cloud app of their maker cannot be added, and Cam Hub offers no sign-in to a cloud account.
Video formatsCam Hub plays H.264 and H.265, decoded in hardware by the phone. A phone without hardware support for H.265, and a picture size above the limit of the decoder, give no picture. MJPEG is used only as a fallback for live view with one of the families.
SoundListening only. G.711 (A-law and µ-law) and AAC-LC are played; any other format is silent. There is no talk-back.
Locked accountsAfter several wrong attempts, a device can lock the account, often for about 30 minutes. Cam Hub stops at the first refused sign-in, and the device report sends no further sign-in after a refusal.
Adding a device againThe same address, HTTP port and username update the stored device instead of creating a second one.

Cameras and recorders

The badge in the device list reads Camera or Recorder. A recorder uses a place in the recorder allowance of the plan, as described in “What uses allowance”. Cam Hub decides as follows.

MethodA device counts as a recorder when
Hikvisionthe device type reported by the device contains NVR or DVR
Dahuathe model name contains NVR, DVR or XVR; otherwise the device is one camera
Synology Surveillance Stationalways; every camera of the system is a channel
ONVIFthe device has more than one separate video source; a camera with several sensors can therefore count as a recorder
Nine RTSP-only brandsthe number in the field Cameras is larger than 1

What to prepare on the device

The following checklist applies to every brand. Items that the device does not have can be skipped.

  • Activate the device and set an administrator password. A new device must be activated before any app can sign in.
  • Give the device a fixed address in the home network, in the device or as a reservation in the router. Cam Hub keeps the address that was entered; see “A device is added, but it is not reachable”.
  • Place the phone and the device in the same network, without a guest network, a separate VLAN, client isolation or a VPN between them.
  • Switch on the HTTP service of the device and note its port, usually 80.
  • Switch on RTSP and note its port, usually 554. Select Digest for RTSP authentication where the device offers the choice.
  • Switch on ONVIF where the device has the setting, and create a separate ONVIF or camera user where the device keeps its own list or the brand requires one.
  • Set the date, the time and the time zone, for example with network time.
  • Set the video to H.264 or H.265, at a moderate resolution, with a key frame interval of one to two seconds. Use a sub stream with a lower resolution for SD where the device offers one.
  • Use an account that may view live video and, for playback, read recordings of the channels that are to be shown.
  • For playback, check that the device records and that a disk or card is present.
  • Note the address, the HTTP port, the RTSP port, the username and the password, which the add-device form asks for.
Devices that cannot be added

A device that works only through the cloud app of its maker, offers no connection on the local network, or accepts HTTPS only, cannot be added to Cam Hub.

The compatibility reference in the app

Path: Devices › ＋ › Add Device › Compatibility reference. The page Compatibility lists what the developer states as supported and not supported.

  • Supported: Hikvision and Dahua, both marked Recommended, then Synology, then SoCatch (iWatch) for the connection on the local network, then Most RTSP cameras and Most ONVIF cameras.
  • Not supported: the connection of SoCatch (iWatch) over the wide area, because it runs through the remote-access service of its maker, which is closed to other apps. Such cameras are to be added on the local network.
  • The Hikvision entry has the button How to keep it off the internet, with notes on keeping a camera without a gateway, on blocking its internet access, and on watching from outside the home network through a private VPN. In some regions, the button or one of the notes is not shown.
  • A note at the bottom states that the names are trademarks of their owners, that Cam Hub is developed independently, and that a successful connection means technical compatibility only.

About this manual

This manual describes Cam Hub 1.5 on iPhone and iPad. Apple TV is covered only in Chapter 14, “Apple TV”.

Scope

  • App and devices: Cam Hub 1.5 on iPhone and iPad. Both run the same app; the manual notes where the two differ. The Apple TV app is not described screen by screen; Chapter 14, “Apple TV” gives the recommended way to bring a setup to it and lists what differs.
  • Content: every function that the app offers to the user is described: adding devices, live view, recording playback, LiveView Mix, control panels, sharing and backup, plans, tools and settings, with the error messages and permission requests that can appear.
  • What the app does not have: Cam Hub is a viewer. It sends no notifications, it has no account of its own, and it uses no cloud service for video. Video travels directly between the device and the iPhone or iPad.
  • Brands: only Chapter 16, “Supported brands and connection methods” names brands. All other chapters describe functions by capability, for example “devices that support playback”.

Conventions

  • Figures: all figures show the English interface with sample data.
  • Labels: names of screens, buttons and settings are written as the app shows them, in the language of this manual, for example Devices. A path such as Settings › About › Version names the screens in the order in which they are opened. When the app is set to another language, its labels differ; the language is chosen in the Settings tab.
  • Typed values: addresses, port numbers and text to be typed are set in a fixed-width type, for example 192.168.1.64 or 554.
  • Procedures: each numbered step is one action. A line that begins with “Check:” states what the screen shows afterwards. A procedure starts with its prerequisites where there are any.
  • Cross-references: a reference to another chapter or section gives its title, and it is a link.

Where to get help

  • Messages, empty screens, permission requests and common questions are explained in Chapter 15, “Troubleshooting”.
  • Failures while adding a device are covered in “When adding fails: the checklist”.
  • How to reach the developer, and what to include in a message, is described in “Reaching the developer”. The support page of the Cam Hub website, support.html, repeats the notes on compatibility and lists the contact address.
